sentences.zh: ○永安王孝基　淮安王神通　 子道彥　孝察　孝同　孝慈　孝友　孝節孝義孝逸

translations.literal: Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji; Prince of Huai'an Shentong; sons Daoyan, Xiaocha, Xiaotong, Xiaoci, Xiaoyou, Xiaojie, Xiaoyi, and Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji; Prince of Huai'an Shentong; and his sons Daoyan, Xiaocha, Xiaotong, Xiaoci, Xiaoyou, Xiaojie, Xiaoyi, and Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 襄邑王神符 子德懋　文暕

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu; sons Demao and Wenliang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu; his sons Demao and Wenliang.

sentences.zh: 長平王叔良 子孝協　孝斌孝斌子思訓思誨　叔良　弟德良　幼良

translations.literal: Prince of Changping Shuliang; sons Xiaoxie and Xiaobin; Xiaobin's sons Sixun and Sihui; Shuliang; younger brothers Deliang and Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changping Shuliang; his sons Xiaoxie and Xiaobin; Xiaobin's sons Sixun and Sihui; Shuliang; and his younger brothers Deliang and Youliang.

sentences.zh: 襄武王琛　河間王孝恭 子晦　孝恭弟　瑊　瑰廬江王瑗 王君廓附

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangwu Chen; Prince of Hejian Xiaogong, son Hui; Xiaogong's younger brothers Jian and Gui; Prince of Lujiang Yuan; with Wang Junkuo appended.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangwu Chen; Prince of Hejian Xiaogong and his son Hui; Xiaogong's younger brothers Jian and Gui; Prince of Lujiang Yuan; with Wang Junkuo appended.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王道玄　江夏王道宗　隴西王博乂宗室永安王孝基永安王孝基，高祖從父弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan; Prince of Jiangxia Daozong; Prince of Longxi Boyi. Imperial Clan: Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji. Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan; Prince of Jiangxia Daozong; Prince of Longxi Boyi. Imperial Clan: Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji. Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 父璋，周梁州刺史，與趙王祐謀殺隋文帝，事洩被誅，高祖即位，追封畢王。

translations.literal: His father Zhang was governor of Liang province under Zhou; he plotted with Prince Zhao You to assassinate Emperor Wen of Sui, but the affair was exposed and he was executed; when Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang had served as governor of Liang province under the Northern Zhou. He joined Prince Zhao You in a plot to kill Emperor Wen of Sui, but the conspiracy was discovered and he was put to death. When Emperor Gaozu came to the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Zhang as Prince of Bi.

sentences.zh: 孝基，武德元年封永安王，歷陝州總管、鴻臚卿，以罪免。

translations.literal: Xiaoji was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong'an in the first year of Wude; he served in turn as commander of Shaan province and as Minister of Ceremonial Reception, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong'an in 618. He served as commander of Shaan province and as Minister of Ceremonial Reception before being dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 二年，劉武周將宋金剛來寇汾、澮。

translations.literal: In the second year, Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang came to raid Fen and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In 619, Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang invaded Fen and Huai.

sentences.zh: 夏縣人呂崇茂殺縣令，舉兵反，自稱魏王，請援於武周。

translations.literal: Lu Chongmao of Xia county killed the magistrate, raised troops in rebellion, styled himself King of Wei, and asked Liu Wuzhou for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chongmao of Xia county killed the magistrate, took up arms in rebellion, proclaimed himself King of Wei, and appealed to Liu Wuzhou for support.

sentences.zh: 復以孝基為行軍總管討之，工部尚書獨孤懷恩、內史侍郎唐儉、陝州總管於筠悉隸焉。

translations.literal: Xiaoji was again appointed campaign commander to suppress him; Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en, Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian, and Shaan commander Yu Jun were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji was again appointed campaign commander to put down the revolt, with Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en, Vice Director of the Secretariat Tang Jian, and Shaan commander Yu Jun all placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 武周遣其將尉遲敬德潛援崇茂，大戰於夏縣，王師敗績，孝基與唐儉等皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou sent his general Yuchi Jingde to secretly reinforce Chongmao; a great battle was fought at Xia county, the imperial army suffered a crushing defeat, and Xiaoji, Tang Jian, and the others all fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou sent his general Yuchi Jingde to reinforce Chongmao in secret. A major battle was fought at Xia county, the imperial army was routed, and Xiaoji, Tang Jian, and the others were all captured by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 後謀歸國，為武周所害，高祖為之發哀，廢朝三日，賜其家帛千匹。

translations.literal: Later he plotted to return to the dynasty and was killed by Liu Wuzhou; Emperor Gaozu mourned him, suspended court for three days, and granted his family one thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted to return to the Tang cause and was killed by Liu Wuzhou. Emperor Gaozu mourned him, suspended court for three days, and granted his family one thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 賊平，購其屍不得，招魂而葬之，贈左衛大將軍，謚曰壯。

translations.literal: When the rebels were suppressed, a reward was offered for his corpse but it could not be found; his spirit was summoned and he was buried, and he was posthumously appointed General of the Left Guard with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated, a reward was offered for his body, but it could not be found. A funeral was held by summoning his spirit home, and he was posthumously appointed General of the Left Guard with the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從兄韶子道立為嗣，封高平郡王。

translations.literal: He had no son; his cousin Shao's son Daoli was made his heir and enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, so his cousin Shao's son Daoli was made his heir and enfeoffed as Prince of Gaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，降為縣公。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was reduced to Duke of a county.
translations.idiomatic: In 626 his rank was reduced to that of a county duke.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，卒於陳州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yonghui era he died while serving as prefect of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yonghui reign he died while serving as prefect of Chen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通淮安王神通，高祖從父弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huai'an Shentong. Prince of Huai'an Shentong was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huai'an Shentong. Prince of Huai'an Shentong was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 父亮，隋海州刺史，武德初追封鄭王。

translations.literal: His father Liang was governor of Hai prefecture under Sui; at the beginning of Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang had served as governor of Hai prefecture under the Sui. At the start of the Wude reign he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 神通，隋末在京師。

translations.literal: Shentong was in the capital at the end of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, Shentong was in the capital.

sentences.zh: 義師起，隋人捕之，神通潛入鄠縣山南，與京師大俠史萬寶、河東裴勣、柳崇禮等舉兵以應義師。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Sui men sought to capture him; Shentong secretly entered the mountains south of Hu county and, with the capital champion Shi Wanbao, Pei Ji of Hedong, Liu Chongli, and others, raised troops in response to the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang uprising began, Sui agents tried to capture him. Shentong slipped into the mountains south of Hu county and, together with the capital champion Shi Wanbao, Pei Ji of Hedong, Liu Chongli, and others, raised troops in support of the cause.

sentences.zh: 遣使與司竹賊帥何潘仁連結。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to join forces with the Sizhu bandit chief He Panren.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to ally with the Sizhu bandit chief He Panren.

sentences.zh: 潘仁奉平陽公主而至，神通與之合勢，進下鄠縣，眾逾一萬。

translations.literal: Panren came leading Princess Pingyang, and Shentong combined forces with them, advanced and took Hu county, and his followers exceeded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Panren arrived leading Princess Pingyang's forces. Shentong joined with them, advanced and captured Hu county, and his army grew to more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 自稱關中道行軍總管，以史萬寶為副，裴勣為長史，柳崇禮為司馬，令狐德棻為記室。

translations.literal: He styled himself campaign commander of the Guanzhong circuit, appointing Shi Wanbao as deputy, Pei Ji as chief administrator, Liu Chongli as marshal, and Linghu Defen as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself campaign commander of the Guanzhong circuit, with Shi Wanbao as his deputy, Pei Ji as chief administrator, Liu Chongli as marshal, and Linghu Defen as recorder.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之大悅，授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu heard this he was greatly pleased and appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased when he heard of this and appointed Shentong Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 從平京師，拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: He followed in the pacification of the capital and was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of the capital and was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，拜右翊衛大將軍，封永康王，尋改封淮安王，為山東道安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was appointed General of the Right Yiyi Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Yongkang, soon changed to Prince of Huai'an, and made Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was appointed General of the Right Yiyi Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Yongkang, soon afterward renamed Prince of Huai'an and made Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 擊宇文化及於魏縣，化及不能抗，東走聊城。

translations.literal: He attacked Yu Wenhuaji at Wei county; Huaji could not resist and fled east to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yu Wenhuaji at Wei county. Huaji could not hold his ground and fled east to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 神通進兵躡之，至聊城。

translations.literal: Shentong advanced in pursuit and reached Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong pressed the pursuit and reached Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 會化及糧盡請降，神通不受。

translations.literal: When Huaji's provisions were exhausted he asked to surrender, but Shentong would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji's supplies ran out he offered to surrender, but Shentong refused.

sentences.zh: 其副使黃門侍郎崔干勸納之，神通曰：「兵士暴露已久，賊計窮糧盡，克在旦暮，正當攻取，以示國威，散其玉帛，以為軍賞。

translations.literal: His deputy, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Cui Gan, urged acceptance; Shentong said: "The soldiers have been exposed to the elements for a long time; the rebels are at their wit's end and out of provisions; capture is imminent. We should attack and take them to display the state's majesty, distribute their treasures and silks, and use them as military rewards.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Cui Gan, urged him to accept the surrender. Shentong said, "Our soldiers have been out in the field for a long time. The enemy is exhausted and out of food; victory is only a matter of days. We should take the city by assault to show the power of the state, seize their treasure and silks, and distribute them as rewards to the army.

sentences.zh: 若受降者，吾何以藉手乎？」

translations.literal: If we accept their surrender, what will we have left to do with our hands?
translations.idiomatic: If we accept their surrender, what will there be left for us to do?

sentences.zh: 干曰：「今建德方至，化及未平，兩賊之間，事必危迫。

translations.literal: Gan said: "Dou Jiande is now arriving, and Huaji is not yet subdued; caught between two enemies, the situation must be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Gan said, "Dou Jiande is on his way, and Huaji is not yet subdued. Caught between two enemies, our position will be desperate.

sentences.zh: 不攻而下之，此勳甚大。

translations.literal: To take them without fighting would be a very great achievement.
translations.idiomatic: To take the city without a fight would be a great achievement.

sentences.zh: 今貪其玉帛，敗無日矣！」

translations.literal: If we now covet their treasures and silks, defeat will come any day!"
translations.idiomatic: If we now grasp for their treasure and silks, defeat will come at any moment!"

sentences.zh: 神通怒，囚干於軍中。

translations.literal: Shentong was angry and imprisoned Gan in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong was furious and had Gan imprisoned in the camp.

sentences.zh: 既而士及自濟北饋之，化及軍稍振，遂拒戰。

translations.literal: Before long Shiji sent supplies from Jibei, Huaji's army gradually revived, and they refused battle and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shiji sent supplies from Jibei, Huaji's army gradually recovered its strength, and they stood firm to fight.

sentences.zh: 神通督兵薄而擊之，貝州刺史趙君德攀堞而上，神通心害其功，因止軍不戰，君德大詬而下，城又堅守。

translations.literal: Shentong urged the troops forward in a close assault; Beizhou prefect Zhao Junde climbed the battlements, but Shentong, jealous of his achievement, halted the army and would not fight; Junde cursed loudly and came down, and the city again held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong pressed the attack at close range. Beizhou prefect Zhao Junde scaled the battlements, but Shentong, resentful of another man's success, halted the army and refused to fight on. Junde cursed him bitterly and climbed back down, and the city continued to hold.

sentences.zh: 神通乃分兵數千人往魏州取攻具，中路復為莘人所敗。

translations.literal: Shentong then detached several thousand men to go to Weizhou for siege equipment, but on the way they were again defeated by men of Shen county.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong then sent several thousand men to Weizhou to fetch siege equipment, but they were ambushed and defeated en route by men from Shen county.

sentences.zh: 竇建德軍且至，遂引軍而退。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande's army was about to arrive, so he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande's army was approaching, so he withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 後二日，化及為建德所虜，賊勢益張，山東城邑多歸建德。

translations.literal: Two days later Huaji was captured by Jiande; the rebel power grew ever stronger, and many cities and towns in Shandong submitted to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Huaji was captured by Jiande. The rebels' power swelled, and many cities and towns in Shandong went over to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 神通兵漸散，退保黎陽，依徐勣，俄為建德所陷。

translations.literal: Shentong's troops gradually dispersed; he withdrew to hold Liyang, relied on Xu Shiji, and soon was captured by Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong's army gradually melted away. He fell back to Liyang and placed himself under Xu Shiji's protection, but soon fell into Jiande's hands.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，復授河北道行台尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Hebei circuit executive.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande's defeat he was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Hebei circuit executive.

sentences.zh: 從太宗平劉黑闥，遷左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Taizong in pacifying Liu Heita and was transferred to General of the Left Wuwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Taizong in the campaign against Liu Heita and was transferred to General of the Left Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，拜開府儀同三司，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and granted five hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: In 627 he was appointed Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and granted an estate of five hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 時太宗謂諸功臣曰：「朕敘公等勳效，量定封邑，恐不能盡當，各自言。」

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Taizong said to the meritorious ministers: "I am ranking your achievements and allotting fiefs, but I fear I may not have done full justice; speak for yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Taizong told his meritorious ministers, "I have ranked your achievements and allotted your fiefs, but I fear I may not have done full justice. Speak for yourselves.

sentences.zh: 神通曰：「義旗初起，臣率兵先至，今房玄齡、杜如晦等刀筆之人，功居第一，臣且不服。」

translations.literal: Shentong said: "When the righteous banner first rose, I led troops and arrived first; now men of the writing brush such as Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui rank first in achievement, and I am not yet satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Shentong said, "When the uprising first began, I was the one who led troops there first. Yet now men of the writing brush such as Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui rank first in merit, and I cannot accept it."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「義旗初起，人皆有心。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When the righteous banner first rose, everyone had the same intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When the uprising first began, everyone had the same intent.

sentences.zh: 叔父雖率兵先至，未嘗身履行陣。

translations.literal: Although Uncle led troops and arrived first, he never personally went into battle.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, though you led troops there first, you never personally took the field.

sentences.zh: 山東未定，受委專征，建德南侵，全軍陷沒；

translations.literal: When Shandong was not yet settled, you were entrusted with independent command; when Jiande invaded from the south, the whole army was lost;
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong was still unsettled, you were entrusted with independent command, yet when Jiande invaded from the south your entire army was lost;

sentences.zh: 及劉黑闥翻動，叔父望風而破。

translations.literal: when Liu Heita stirred up trouble, Uncle's forces collapsed at the mere sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: and when Liu Heita rose in revolt, your forces collapsed at the mere sight of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今計勳行賞，玄齡等有籌謀帷幄定社稷功，所以漢之蕭何，雖無汗馬，指縱推轂，故功居第一。

translations.literal: Now in reckoning merit and granting rewards, Xuanling and the others have the achievement of planning within the tent to settle the realm; they are like Xiao He of Han—though without sweat-stained horses, they directed and pushed the chariot wheel, and therefore rank first in merit.
translations.idiomatic: In reckoning merit and granting rewards today, Xuanling and the others deserve first place for the achievement of planning within the tent to secure the realm. They are like Xiao He of Han: though they never rode sweating horses into battle, they directed strategy from behind the lines, and so their merit ranks first.

sentences.zh: 叔父於國至親，誠無所愛，必不可緣私濫與勳臣同賞耳。」

translations.literal: Uncle is the closest of kin to the state; I truly hold nothing back, but you must not on account of private feeling be indiscriminately granted the same rewards as meritorious ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, you are the closest of kin to the throne, and I withhold nothing from you in my heart—but you cannot on account of family feeling be indiscriminately granted the same rewards as the meritorious ministers."

sentences.zh: 四年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In 630 he died.

sentences.zh: 太宗為之廢朝，贈司空，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong suspended court for him, posthumously appointed him Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong suspended court in mourning for him, posthumously appointed him Minister of Works, and gave him the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔與河間王孝恭、贈陝州大行台右僕射鄖節公殷開山、贈民部尚書渝襄公劉政會配饗高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict ordered that he, together with Prince of Hejian Xiaogong, the posthumously honored Right Vice Director of the Shaan executive Yin Kaishan, Duke of Yun with posthumous title Jie, and the posthumously honored Minister of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, Duke of Yu with posthumous title Xiang, be granted joint sacrifice in the ancestral temple of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In 640 an edict ordered that he, together with Prince of Hejian Xiaogong, the posthumously honored Right Vice Director of the Shaan executive Yin Kaishan, Duke of Yun with posthumous title Jie, and the posthumously honored Minister of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, Duke of Yu with posthumous title Xiang, receive joint sacrifice in Emperor Gaozu's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 有子十一人：長子道彥，武德五年，封膠東王；

translations.literal: He had eleven sons: the eldest son Daoyan, in the fifth year of Wude enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaodong;
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons. The eldest, Daoyan, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiaodong in 622;

sentences.zh: 次孝察，高密王；

translations.literal: the next Xiaocha, Prince of Gaomi;
translations.idiomatic: the next, Xiaocha, Prince of Gaomi;

sentences.zh: 孝同，淄川王；

translations.literal: Xiaotong, Prince of Zichuan;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaotong, Prince of Zichuan;

sentences.zh: 孝慈，廣平王；

translations.literal: Xiaoci, Prince of Guangping;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci, Prince of Guangping;

sentences.zh: 孝友，河間王；

translations.literal: Xiaoyou, Prince of Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou, Prince of Hejian;

sentences.zh: 孝節，清河王；

translations.literal: Xiaojie, Prince of Qinghe;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie, Prince of Qinghe;

sentences.zh: 孝義，膠西王。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi, Prince of Jiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiaoyi, Prince of Jiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖受禪，以天下未定，廣封宗室以威天下，皇從弟及侄年始孩童者數十人，皆封為郡王。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, because the realm was not yet settled he broadly enfeoffed members of the imperial clan to awe the world; several dozen paternal cousins and nephews who were still children were all enfeoffed as princes of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Emperor Gaozu took the throne, the realm was still unsettled, so he broadly enfeoffed members of the imperial clan to overawe the empire. Several dozen paternal cousins and nephews who were still children were all made princes of commanderies.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，因舉宗正屬藉問侍臣曰：「遍封宗子，於天下便乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he raised the imperial clan register kept by the Director of the Imperial Clan and asked the attending ministers: "Is it convenient for the realm to enfeoff imperial clansmen so broadly?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, he took up the imperial clan register kept by the Director of the Imperial Clan and asked his ministers, "Is it good for the realm to enfeoff imperial clansmen so broadly?

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射封德彝對曰：「歷觀往古，封王者，今最為多。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Deyi replied: "Looking through past ages, those enfeoffed as kings today are the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Feng Deyi replied, "Looking through history, never have so many been enfeoffed as kings as today.

sentences.zh: 兩漢已降，唯封帝子及親兄弟，若宗室疏遠者，非有大功如周之郇、滕，漢之賈、澤，並不得濫封，所以別親疏也。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties onward, only the emperor's sons and close brothers were enfeoffed; if members of the imperial clan were more distant, unless they had great merit like Xun and Teng of Zhou or Jia and Ze of Han, they were not indiscriminately enfeoffed—this was to distinguish near from far kin.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han dynasties onward, only the emperor's sons and close brothers were enfeoffed as kings. More distant members of the imperial clan were not enfeoffed indiscriminately unless they had great merit, as with Xun and Teng under Zhou or Jia and Ze under Han. That was how near and distant kin were distinguished.

sentences.zh: 先朝惇睦九族，一切封王，爵命既隆，多給力役，蓋以天下為私，殊非至公馭物之道。」

translations.literal: The previous court treated the nine clans with affection and enfeoffed them all as kings; once their titles were lofty, many were given corvée labor—this treated the realm as private property and was far from the way of utmost fairness in governing all things."
translations.idiomatic: The previous court, in the name of cherishing the nine clans, enfeoffed them all as kings. Once their titles were raised so high, many were burdened with corvée labor. That treated the realm as private property and was far from the way of governing all under Heaven with utmost fairness."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「朕理天下，本為百姓，非欲勞百姓以養己之親也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "I govern the realm for the sake of the common people; I do not wish to burden the common people to support my own kin."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong said, "I govern the realm for the sake of the people. I do not wish to burden the people in order to support my own kin."

sentences.zh: 於是宗室率以屬疏降爵為郡公，唯有功者數十人封王。

translations.literal: Thereupon the imperial clan, for the most part because of distant kinship, had their ranks reduced to dukes of commanderies; only several dozen men with achievement were enfeoffed as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon most members of the imperial clan, on account of distant kinship, had their ranks reduced to commandery dukes, and only several dozen men with real achievement were enfeoffed as kings.

sentences.zh: 是時道彥等並隨例降爵。

translations.literal: At that time Daoyan and the others all had their ranks reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Daoyan and the others all had their ranks reduced along with the rest.

sentences.zh: 道彥與季弟孝逸最知名。

translations.literal: Daoyan and his youngest brother Xiaoyi were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan and his youngest brother Xiaoyi were the best known among them.

sentences.zh: 道彥幼而事親甚謹。

translations.literal: Daoyan from youth served his parents with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Daoyan served his parents with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 初，義師起，神通逃難，被疾於山谷，綿曆數旬，山中食盡。

translations.literal: At first, when the righteous army rose, Shentong fled into hiding, fell ill in the mountains and valleys, and remained there for several tens of days until food in the mountains was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising first began, Shentong fled into hiding and fell ill in the mountains. He remained there for weeks until the food in the hills ran out.

sentences.zh: 道彥著故弊衣，出人間乞丐，及采野實，以供其父，身無所啖。

translations.literal: Daoyan wore old worn-out clothes, went among people to beg, and gathered wild fruits to supply his father, eating nothing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan put on old, tattered clothes, went among people to beg, and gathered wild fruits to feed his father, keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 其父分以食之，輒詐言已啖，而覆藏留之，以備闕乏。

translations.literal: When his father shared food with him to eat, he would falsely say he had already eaten, then secretly hide and keep it to guard against want.
translations.idiomatic: When his father tried to share food with him, he would claim he had already eaten, then secretly hide what he was given to save for later need.

sentences.zh: 及神通應義舉，授朝請大夫。

translations.literal: When Shentong responded to the righteous uprising, Daoyan was appointed Gentleman for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Shentong joined the uprising, Daoyan was appointed Gentleman for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，封義興郡公，進封膠東王，授隴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Daoyan was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing commandery, advanced to Prince of Jiaodong, and appointed prefect of Long prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, Daoyan was enfeoffed as Duke of Yixing commandery, then advanced to Prince of Jiaodong and appointed prefect of Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，轉相州都督，例降爵為公，拜岷州都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred to commissioner of Xiang prefecture, had his rank reduced by precedent to duke, and was appointed commissioner of Min prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he was transferred to commissioner of Xiang prefecture, had his rank reduced to duke under the general precedent, and was appointed commissioner of Min prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，廬於墓側，負土成墳，躬植松柏，容貌哀毀，親友皆不復識之。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he mourned, built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to form the mound, personally planted pines and cypresses, and his appearance was so wasted by grief that relatives and friends no longer recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning, built a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to raise the mound, and personally planted pines and cypresses. Grief so wasted his appearance that relatives and friends no longer recognized him.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而嘉嘆，令侍中王珪就加開喻。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong heard this he praised and sighed, and ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui to go and offer further consolation and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of this he praised him warmly and sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui to offer further consolation and guidance.

sentences.zh: 復授岷州都督。

translations.literal: He was again appointed commissioner of Min prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed commissioner of Min prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道彥遣使告喻党項諸部，申國威靈，多有降附。

translations.literal: Daoyan sent envoys to announce and instruct the various Tangut tribes, displaying the state's majesty and power, and many submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan sent envoys to announce the Tang's authority to the various Tangut tribes, and many submitted.

sentences.zh: 李靖之擊吐谷渾也，詔道彥為赤水道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, an edict appointed Daoyan campaign commander of the Chishui route.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing attacked Tuyuhun, an edict appointed Daoyan campaign commander of the Chishui route.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷復厚幣遺党項，令為鄉導，党項首領拓拔赤辭來詣靖軍，請諸將曰：「往者隋人來擊吐谷渾，我党項每資軍用，而隋人無信，必見侵掠。

translations.literal: At that time the court again sent rich gifts to the Tangut and ordered them to serve as guides; the Tangut chieftain Tuo Ba Chici came to Li Jing's army and said to the generals: "In the past when Sui men came to attack Tuyuhun, we Tangut always supplied the army's needs, yet the Sui were faithless and always invaded and plundered us.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court again sent rich gifts to the Tangut and ordered them to serve as guides. The Tangut chieftain Tuo Ba Chici came to Li Jing's camp and told the generals, "In the past, whenever Sui forces came to attack Tuyuhun, we Tangut supplied their armies, yet the Sui were faithless and always invaded and plundered us.

sentences.zh: 今將軍若無他心者，我當資給糧運；

translations.literal: If the general now has no other intent, we will supply grain transport;
translations.idiomatic: If you, General, have no other designs, we will supply grain for your transport;

sentences.zh: 如或我欺，當即固險以塞軍路。」

translations.literal: but if we are deceived, we will immediately hold the passes and block the army's route.
translations.idiomatic: but if we are deceived, we will immediately hold the passes and block your army's route.

sentences.zh: 諸將與之歃血而盟，赤辭信之。

translations.literal: The generals drank blood with him in alliance, and Chici trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: The generals drank blood with him in alliance, and Chici trusted them.

sentences.zh: 道彥既至闊水，見赤辭無備，遂襲之，虜牛羊數千頭。

translations.literal: When Daoyan reached Kuoshui and saw that Chici was unprepared, he attacked him and captured several thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyan reached Kuoshui and saw that Chici was unprepared, he attacked him and seized several thousand head of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 於是諸羌怨怒，屯兵野狐硤，道彥不能進，為赤辭所乘，軍大敗，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various Qiang were resentful and angry, massed troops at Yehu Gorge, and Daoyan could not advance; Chici seized the opportunity, the army suffered a great defeat, and tens of thousands died.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang tribes were enraged and massed troops at Yehu Gorge. Daoyan could not advance, Chici seized the opportunity, and the army was routed with tens of thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 道彥退保松州，竟坐減死徙邊。

translations.literal: Daoyan withdrew to hold Song prefecture; in the end he was sentenced to commuted death and exile to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan withdrew to Song prefecture. In the end he was sentenced to commuted death and exile to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 後起為涼州都督，尋卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled and appointed commissioner of Liang prefecture; soon afterward he died and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled and appointed commissioner of Liang prefecture. He died soon afterward and was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孝逸少好學，解屬文。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiaoyi loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 初封梁郡公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke of Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高宗末，歷給事中，四遷益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign he served in turn as Supervising Attendant and was promoted four times to chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Gaozong's reign he served as Supervising Attendant and rose through four promotions to chief administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，入為左衛將軍，甚見親遇。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court, he entered service as General of the Left Guard and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed power, he entered court service as General of the Left Guard and enjoyed great favor.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，徐敬業據揚州作亂，以孝逸為左玉鈐衛大將軍、揚州行軍大總管，督軍以討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangzhai, Xu Jingye seized Yangzhou and rebelled; Xiaoyi was appointed General of the Left Yuling Guard and Grand Campaign Commander of Yangzhou to supervise the army in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 Xu Jingye seized Yangzhou and rebelled. Xiaoyi was appointed General of the Left Yuling Guard and Grand Campaign Commander of Yangzhou to lead the army against him.

sentences.zh: 孝逸引軍至淮，而敬業方南攻潤州，遣其弟敬猷屯兵淮陰；

translations.literal: Xiaoyi led the army to the Huai River, while Jingye was then attacking Runzhou to the south and sent his younger brother Jingyou to encamp at Huaiyin;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi led his army to the Huai River. Jingye was then attacking Runzhou to the south and had sent his younger brother Jingyou to encamp at Huaiyin;

sentences.zh: 偽將韋超據都梁山，以拒孝逸。

translations.literal: the rebel general Wei Chao held Duliang Mountain to resist Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: while the rebel general Wei Chao held Duliang Mountain to block Xiaoyi's advance.

sentences.zh: 裨將馬敬臣擊斬賊之別帥尉遲昭、夏侯瓚等，超乃擁眾憑山以自固。

translations.literal: Lieutenant general Ma Jingchen attacked and killed the rebels' secondary commanders Yuchi Zhao, Xiahou Zan, and others; Chao then gathered his followers and relied on the mountain to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant general Ma Jingchen attacked and killed the rebel secondary commanders Yuchi Zhao, Xiahou Zan, and others. Chao then gathered his forces on the mountain and dug in.

sentences.zh: 或謂孝逸曰：「超眾守險，且憑山為阻，攻之則士無所施其力，騎無所騁其足，窮寇殊死，殺傷必眾。

translations.literal: Someone said to Xiaoyi: "Chao's force holds the passes and relies on the mountain as a barrier; if we attack, the infantry will have nowhere to exert their strength and the cavalry nowhere to gallop their hooves; cornered rebels will fight to the death, and casualties must be heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Xiaoyi, "Chao's force holds the passes and uses the mountain as a barrier. If we attack, the infantry will have no room to exert themselves and the cavalry no room to charge. Cornered rebels will fight to the death, and our casualties will be heavy.

sentences.zh: 不若分兵守之，大軍直趣揚州，未數日，其勢必降也。」

translations.literal: It would be better to divide troops to contain them while the main army strikes straight for Yangzhou; within a few days their force will surely submit.
translations.idiomatic: Better to detach troops to contain them while the main army marches straight on Yangzhou. In a few days their resistance will surely collapse.

sentences.zh: 支度使、廣府司馬薛克構曰：「超雖據險，其卒非多，今逢小寇不擊，何以示武？

translations.literal: Support-Distribution Commissioner and Guang Prefecture Vice-Marshal Xue Ke Gou said: "Although Chao holds the passes, his troops are not numerous. If we meet a small band of rebels and do not strike, how can we display martial prowess?
translations.idiomatic: Support-Distribution Commissioner and Guang Prefecture Vice-Marshal Xue Ke Gou said, "Although Chao holds the passes, his troops are not numerous. If we encounter a small rebel band and fail to attack, how can we demonstrate our martial prowess?

sentences.zh: 若加兵以守，則有闕前機；

translations.literal: If we add troops to garrison them, we will miss the earlier opportunity;
translations.idiomatic: If we detach troops to garrison them, we will miss our chance;

sentences.zh: 舍之而前，則終為後患，不如擊之。

translations.literal: if we leave them and advance, they will ultimately become a later threat — better to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: if we leave them and press on, they will become a threat in our rear. We should attack them.

sentences.zh: 克超則淮陰自懾，淮陰破，則楚州諸縣必開門而候官軍。

translations.literal: Defeat Chao and Huaiyin will itself be intimidated; when Huaiyin falls, the various counties of Chu prefecture will surely open their gates and await the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Defeat Chao and Huaiyin will lose heart on its own. Once Huaiyin falls, every county in Chu prefecture will open its gates to the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 然後進兵高郵，直趣江都，逆豎之首，可指掌而懸也。」

translations.literal: Then advance troops to Gaoyou and strike straight for Jiangdu — the rebel chieftain's head can be taken as easily as pointing at one's palm and hanging it up.
translations.idiomatic: Then we can advance on Gaoyou and strike straight for Jiangdu. The rebel leader's head will be ours for the taking.

sentences.zh: 孝逸從其言，進兵擊超賊，眾壓伏，官軍登山急擊之，殺數百人，日暮圍解，超銜枚夜遁。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi followed his advice, advanced to attack Chao's rebels; the force pressed down from above, the imperial army climbed the mountain and pressed the attack, killing several hundred; at dusk the siege was lifted, and Chao fled by night with gags in the soldiers' mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi followed his counsel and advanced against Chao's rebels. Pressing down from the heights, the imperial army stormed the mountain and killed several hundred. At dusk the siege lifted, and Chao slipped away in silence under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 孝逸引兵擊淮陰，大破敬猷之眾。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi led troops to attack Huaiyin and routed Jingyou's force.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi led his troops against Huaiyin and routed Jingyou's army.

sentences.zh: 時敬業回軍屯於下阿溪以拒官軍，有流星墜其營。

translations.literal: At the time Jingye recalled his army and encamped at Xia'a Creek to resist the imperial army; a shooting star fell on his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye had recalled his army and encamped at Xia'a Creek to block the imperial advance when a shooting star fell on his camp.

sentences.zh: 孝逸引兵渡溪以擊之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi led troops across the creek to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi led his troops across the creek to attack him.

sentences.zh: 敬業初勝後敗，孝逸乘勝追奔數十里，敬業窘迫，與其黨攜妻子逃入海曲。

translations.literal: Jingye was first victorious then defeated; Xiaoyi pursued the fleeing enemy in victory for several tens of li; Jingye was hard pressed and fled with his followers, bringing their wives and children, into a coastal inlet.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye won the opening clash but lost the next. Xiaoyi pursued the fleeing rebels for dozens of li. Hard pressed, Jingye fled with his followers and their families into a coastal inlet.

sentences.zh: 孝逸進據揚州，盡捕斬敬業等，振旅而還，以功進授鎮軍大將軍，轉左豹韜衛大將軍，改封吳國公。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi advanced and seized Yangzhou, captured and executed Jingye and the rest, shook out his ranks and returned; for his merit he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, transferred to General of the Left Leopard Bow Guard, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Wu state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi advanced into Yangzhou, captured and executed Jingye and his followers, and returned in triumph. For his service he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, transferred to General of the Left Leopard Bow Guard, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 孝逸素有名望，自是時譽益重，武承嗣等深所忌嫉，數讒毀之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi had long enjoyed renown; from this time his contemporary reputation grew even weightier; Wu Chengsi and others deeply envied and resented him and repeatedly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi had long enjoyed a high reputation, and from this victory his standing grew even greater. Wu Chengsi and his faction deeply envied him and repeatedly slandered him.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年，左遷施州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong, he was demoted to prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: In 686 he was demoted to prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 其冬，承嗣等又使人誣告孝逸往任益州，嘗自解「逸」字云：「走繞兔者，常在月中。

translations.literal: That winter, Chengsi and others again sent men to falsely accuse Xiaoyi: during his earlier tenure in Yizhou he had once explained the character for Yi, saying, "One who runs after rabbits is always in the moon.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chengsi and his allies sent men to accuse Xiaoyi falsely. They claimed that while serving in Yizhou he had once parsed the character for his name Yi, saying, "To run after a rabbit is always to be in the moon.

sentences.zh: 月既近天，合有天分。」

translations.literal: The moon is close to heaven — he ought to have a heavenly portion."
translations.idiomatic: The moon is near heaven — he was therefore destined for imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 則天以孝逸常有功，減死配徙儋州，尋卒。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, because Xiaoyi had often rendered merit, commuted death to exile at Dan prefecture; soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, because Xiaoyi had often rendered great service, commuted his death sentence to exile in Dan prefecture. He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，贈益州大都督。

translations.literal: Early in Jingyun, he was posthumously appointed metropolitan overseer of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun era he was posthumously appointed metropolitan overseer of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝銳孫齊物，孝同曾孫國貞，別有傳。

translations.literal: Xiaorui's grandson Qiwu and Xiaotong's great-grandson Guozhen have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaorui's grandson Qiwu and Xiaotong's great-grandson Guozhen have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 襄邑王神符，神通弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu was the younger brother of Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangyi Shenfu was the younger brother of Shentong.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事兄以友悌聞。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he was known for treating his elder brother with friendship and fraternal respect.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was known for the friendship and fraternal devotion he showed his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 義寧初，授光祿大夫，封安吉郡公。

translations.literal: Early in Yining, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Anji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yining era he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Anji commandery.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，進封襄邑郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he was advanced to Prince of Xiangyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was promoted to Prince of Xiangyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，累遷并州總管。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after successive promotions he became area commander of Bing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 621, after a series of promotions, he became area commander of Bing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗率眾來寇，神符出兵與戰於汾水東，敗之，斬首五百級，虜其馬二千匹。

translations.literal: The Türk khagan Jieli led his host to raid; Shenfu deployed troops and fought east of the Fen River, defeated them, took five hundred heads, and captured two thousand of their horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Türk khagan Jieli led a raid, Shenfu took the field and fought him east of the Fen River. He routed the Türks, took five hundred heads, and captured two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 又戰於沙河之北，獲其乙利達官並可汗所乘馬及甲獻之，由是召拜太府卿。

translations.literal: Again he fought north of the Sha River, captured their elite commander Yili and the khagan's own horse and armor, which he presented; for this he was summoned and appointed Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again north of the Sha River, captured the Türk elite commander Yili along with the khagan's horse and armor, and presented them as trophies. He was then summoned to court and appointed Director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷揚州大都督，移州府及居人自丹陽渡江，州人賴焉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to metropolitan overseer of Yang prefecture; he moved the prefectural seat and its residents across the river from Danyang — the people of the prefecture relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: In 626 he was transferred to metropolitan overseer of Yang prefecture. He moved the prefectural seat and its residents across the river from Danyang, to the great benefit of the region.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，再遷宗正卿。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, he was again transferred to Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he was again transferred, becoming Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 後以疾辭職，太宗幸其第問疾，賜以縑帛，每給羊酒。

translations.literal: Later he resigned office because of illness; Emperor Taizong visited his residence to inquire after his illness, bestowed silk and brocade on him, and regularly supplied mutton and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resigned because of illness. Emperor Taizong visited his home to inquire after him, bestowed silk and brocade, and regularly sent mutton and wine.

sentences.zh: 又令乘小輿，引入紫微殿，以神符腳疾，乃遣三衛輿之而升。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to ride in a small palanquin and was brought into the Ziwei Hall; because Shenfu had foot ailment, the Three Guards were sent to carry him in a litter up the steps.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to ride in a small palanquin and was brought into the Ziwei Hall. Because Shenfu suffered from foot ailment, the Three Guards carried him up in a litter.

sentences.zh: 尋授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was granted the ceremonial rank of Grand Master with Privileges Equal to Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted the ceremonial rank of Grand Master with Privileges Equal to Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年薨，年七十三，贈司空、荊州都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he died at age seventy-three; posthumously appointed Minister of Works and commissioner of Jing prefecture, buried with Xian mausoleum, posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 651 at the age of seventy-three. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and commissioner of Jing prefecture, buried with Emperor Gaozu's Xian mausoleum, and given the posthumous title Gong, Respectful.

sentences.zh: 有子七人，武德初，並封郡王，後例降封縣公。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; early in Wude all were enfeoffed as commandery princes, then by precedent demoted to county marquises.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons. Early in Wude all were enfeoffed as commandery princes, then later demoted by precedent to county marquises.

sentences.zh: 次子德懋、少子文暕最知名。

translations.literal: His second son Demao and youngest son Wenliang were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Demao and youngest son Wenliang were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 德懋官至少府監、臨川郡公。

translations.literal: Demao rose to Director of the Lesser Treasury and Duke of Linchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Demao rose to Director of the Lesser Treasury and Duke of Linchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 文暕歷幽州都督、魏郡公。

translations.literal: Wenliang served in turn as commissioner of You prefecture and Duke of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wenliang served in turn as commissioner of You prefecture and Duke of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，坐事貶為藤州別駕，尋被誅。

translations.literal: During Chuigong, for an offense he was demoted to deputy prefect of Teng prefecture; soon afterward he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong era he was demoted to deputy prefect of Teng prefecture for an offense and was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 文暕子佺，開元中為宗正卿。

translations.literal: Wenliang's son Quan, during Kaiyuan, served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wenliang's son Quan served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 長平王叔良長平王叔良，高祖從父弟也。

translations.literal: Prince of Changping Shuliang — Prince of Changping Shuliang was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Changping Shuliang — Prince of Changping Shuliang was a paternal cousin of Emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 父禕，隋上儀同三司，武德初，追封郇王。

translations.literal: His father Yi held the Sui rank of Senior Master of Ceremony of the Third Rank; early in Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had held the Sui rank of Senior Master of Ceremony of the Third Rank. Early in Wude he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xun.

sentences.zh: 叔良，義寧中授左光祿大夫，封長平郡公。

translations.literal: Shuliang, during Yining, was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yining era Shuliang was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed as Duke of Changping commandery.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，拜刑部侍郎，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and advanced in rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and promoted to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 師鎮涇州，以御薛舉。

translations.literal: He led troops garrisoning Jing prefecture to guard against Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He took command at Jing prefecture to guard against Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 舉乃陽言食盡，引兵南去，遣高墌人偽以降。

translations.literal: Ju then falsely claimed his provisions were exhausted, led his troops southward, and sent a man from Gaodi to feign surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ju then falsely claimed his provisions were exhausted, withdrew south, and sent a man from Gaodi to offer a fake surrender.

sentences.zh: 叔良遣驃騎劉感率眾赴之，至百里細川，伏兵發，官軍敗績，劉感沒於陣。

translations.literal: Shuliang sent swift-cavalry commander Liu Gan to lead troops to meet them; when they reached Baili Xichuan, ambush troops sprang up, the imperial army suffered defeat, and Liu Gan perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang sent swift-cavalry commander Liu Gan to meet them. At Baili Xichuan an ambush sprang up, the imperial army was routed, and Liu Gan fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 叔良大懼，出金以賜士卒。

translations.literal: Shuliang was greatly frightened and distributed gold to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang was terrified and distributed gold to reward his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 嚴為守備，涇州僅全。

translations.literal: He tightened defenses; Jing prefecture barely survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened the defenses, and Jing prefecture barely held.

sentences.zh: 四年，突厥入寇，命叔良率五軍擊之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the Türks raided, Shuliang was ordered to lead five armies to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In 621, when the Türks raided, Shuliang was ordered to lead five armies against them.

sentences.zh: 叔良中流矢而薨，贈左翊衛大將軍、靈州總管，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: Shuliang was struck by a stray arrow and died; posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard and area commander of Ling prefecture, posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang was struck by a stray arrow and died. He was posthumously appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard and area commander of Ling prefecture, with the posthumous title Su, Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子孝協嗣，武德五年，封范陽郡王。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoxie succeeded; in the fifth year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoxie succeeded him. In 622 he was enfeoffed as Prince of Fanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，以屬疏例降封郇國公，累遷魏州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, by the precedent for distant kin his rank was reduced to Duke of Xun state; after successive promotions he became prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, by the precedent for more distant imperial kin, his rank was reduced to Duke of Xun. He later rose through successive promotions to prefect of Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，坐受贓賜死。

translations.literal: During Linde, for accepting bribes he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: During the Linde era he was sentenced to death for accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 孝協弟孝斌，官至原州都督府長史。

translations.literal: Xiaoxie's younger brother Xiaobin rose to chief administrator of the Yuan prefecture commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxie's younger brother Xiaobin rose to chief administrator of the Yuan prefecture commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 孝斌子思訓，高宗時累轉江都令。

translations.literal: Xiaobin's son Sixun, during Emperor Gaozong's reign, rose through successive transfers to magistrate of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobin's son Sixun, during Emperor Gaozong's reign, rose through successive appointments to magistrate of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 屬則天革命，宗室多見搆陷，思訓遂棄官潛匿。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu changed the dynasty, many of the imperial clan were framed and trapped; Sixun then resigned his office and went into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu seized power, many members of the imperial clan were framed. Sixun resigned his office and went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，中宗初復宗社，以思訓舊齒，驟遷宗正卿，封隴西郡公，實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, when Emperor Zhongzong first restored the state altars, because Sixun was a senior member of the clan he was suddenly promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court, enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery with two hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era, when Emperor Zhongzong restored the Tang dynasty, Sixun was suddenly promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court and enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi commandery with an income of two hundred households, in recognition of his senior standing in the clan.

sentences.zh: 歷益州長史。

translations.literal: He served as chief administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，左羽林大將軍，進封彭國公，更加實封二百戶，尋轉右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, he was General of the Left Forest Guard, advanced to Duke of Peng state with an additional two hundred taxable households, soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he was General of the Left Forest Guard, then promoted to Duke of Peng with an additional two hundred taxable households, and soon transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 718.

sentences.zh: 贈秦州都督，陪葬橋陵。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed commissioner of Qin prefecture, buried with Qiao mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed commissioner of Qin prefecture and buried with Emperor Ruizong's Qiao mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 思訓尤善丹青，迄今繪事者推李將軍山水。

translations.literal: Sixun was especially skilled at painting; to this day painters praise General Li's landscape art.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun was especially skilled at painting. To this day painters speak of "General Li's landscapes" — the style he himself made famous.

sentences.zh: 思訓弟思誨，垂拱中揚州參軍。

translations.literal: Sixun's younger brother Sihui, during Chuigong, was an aide in Yang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun's younger brother Sihui served as an aide in Yang prefecture during the Chuigong era.

sentences.zh: 思誨子林甫別有傳。

translations.literal: Sihui's son Linpu has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui's son Linpu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 叔良弟德良，少有疾，不仕。

translations.literal: Shuliang's younger brother Deliang had illness from youth and did not serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shuliang's younger brother Deliang had been ill from youth and never held office.

sentences.zh: 武德初，封新興王。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十一年薨，贈涼州都督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhenguan he died; posthumously appointed commissioner of Liang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 637 and was posthumously appointed commissioner of Liang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德良孫晉，先天中，為殿中監，兼雍州長史，甚有威名，紹封新興王。

translations.literal: Deliang's grandson Jin, during Xiantian, served as Director of the Palace Administration and concurrent chief administrator of Yong prefecture; he enjoyed great renown and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Deliang's grandson Jin, during the Xiantian era, served as Director of the Palace Administration and concurrent chief administrator of Yong prefecture. He enjoyed great renown and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 尋坐附會太平公主伏誅，改姓厲氏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward for associating with Princess Taiping he was executed; his surname was changed to Li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was executed for associating with Princess Taiping, and his clan surname was changed to Li.

sentences.zh: 初，晉之就誅，僚吏皆奔散，唯司功李捴步從，不失在官之禮，仍哭其屍。

translations.literal: When Jin was about to be executed, his staff officials all fled; only Records Officer Li Zong followed on foot, never failing the decorum of office, and still wept over his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was about to be executed, his staff officials all fled. Only Records Officer Li Zong followed on foot, observing every propriety of office, and wept over his corpse.

sentences.zh: 姚崇聞之曰：「欒、向之儔也。」

translations.literal: Yao Chong heard of this and said: "A companion of Luan and Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong heard of this, he said, "He is of the same breed as Luan and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to a Secretariat Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to a Secretariat officer.

sentences.zh: 後官至澤州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he rose to prefect of Ze.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to prefect of Ze.

sentences.zh: 德良弟幼良，武德初，封長樂王。

translations.literal: Deliang's younger brother Youliang, early in Wude, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Deliang's younger brother Youliang was enfeoffed as Prince of Changle early in Wude.

sentences.zh: 時有人盜其馬者，幼良獲盜而閃殺之，高祖怒曰：「昔人賜盜馬者酒，終獲其報，爾輒行戮，何無古風！

translations.literal: Once when someone stole his horse, Youliang captured the thief and killed him on the spot; Emperor Gaozu was angry and said: "In olden days men gave wine to one who stole their horses, and in the end received repayment — you rashly carried out execution; where is the ancient spirit!
translations.idiomatic: Once when someone stole his horse, Youliang captured the thief and killed him on the spot. Emperor Gaozu was furious and said, "In antiquity a man who had his horse stolen would treat the thief to wine and in the end receive his reward. You executed the man outright — where is the spirit of the ancients!

sentences.zh: 盜者信有罪矣，專殺豈非枉邪？」

translations.literal: A thief is indeed guilty — but is summary killing not injustice?
translations.idiomatic: The thief was indeed guilty, but is summary execution not itself a wrong?

sentences.zh: 遣禮部尚書李綱於朝堂集宗室王公而撻之。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Rites Li Gang to assemble the princes and nobles of the imperial clan in the court hall and have him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of Rites Li Gang to assemble the princes and nobles of the imperial clan in the court hall and have Youliang flogged.

sentences.zh: 自後累遷涼州都督，嘗引不逞百餘人為左右，多侵暴市裡，行旅苦之。

translations.literal: Afterward he rose through successive transfers to commissioner of Liang prefecture; he once retained more than a hundred unruly men as his close retainers, who frequently plundered the markets — travelers suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he rose through successive appointments to commissioner of Liang prefecture. He kept more than a hundred unruly men as personal retainers, and they frequently terrorized the markets. Travelers suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，有告幼良陰養死士，交通境外，恐謀為反叛，詔遣中書令宇文士及代為都督，並按其事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, someone reported that Youliang secretly nurtured desperate fighters, maintained contact beyond the border, and might plot rebellion; an edict sent Chief Councillor Yuwen Shiji to replace him as commissioner and investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, someone reported that Youliang was secretly training desperate men and maintaining contacts beyond the border, possibly plotting rebellion. An edict sent Chief Councillor Yuwen Shiji to replace him as commissioner and investigate.

sentences.zh: 士及慮其為變，遂縊殺之。

translations.literal: Shiji feared he might rebel and strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a revolt, Shiji had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 襄武王琛襄武王琛，高祖從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Xiangwu Chen — Prince of Xiangwu Chen was a son of Emperor Gaozu's paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xiangwu Chen — Prince of Xiangwu Chen was a son of Emperor Gaozu's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖蔚，周朔州總管。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wei was area commander of Shuo prefecture under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wei had been area commander of Shuo prefecture under the Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父安，隋領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: His father An was General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father An had been General-in-Chief of the Palace Guard under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 武德初，追封蔚為蔡王，安為西平王。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, Wei was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai and An as Prince of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude, Wei was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cai and An as Prince of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 琛，義寧中封襄武郡公，與太常卿鄭元璹齎女妓遺突厥始畢可汗，以結和親。

translations.literal: Chen, during Yining, was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu commandery; together with Director of Ceremonial Zheng Yuanshang he brought female entertainers as gifts to the Türk khagan Shibi to forge a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yining era Chen was enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangwu commandery. Together with Director of Ceremonial Zheng Yuanshang he brought female entertainers as gifts to the Türk khagan Shibi to cement a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 始畢甚重之，贈名馬數百匹，遣骨咄祿特勒隨琛貢方物。

translations.literal: Shibi held them in great esteem, bestowed several hundred famous horses, and sent the Türk noble Kutlug Tegin to follow Chen in presenting tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi received them with great honor, bestowed several hundred fine horses, and sent the Türk noble Kutlug Tegin to accompany Chen in presenting tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，拜刑部侍郎，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased, appointed him Vice Minister of Justice, and advanced his rank to prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased. He appointed Chen Vice Minister of Justice and promoted him to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 歷蒲、絳二州總管。

translations.literal: He served in turn as area commander of Pu and Jiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as area commander of Pu and Jiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及宋金剛陷澮州，時稽胡多叛，轉琛為隰州總管以鎮之。

translations.literal: When Song Jingang took Fen prefecture, and many Jié-Xiongnu peoples were rebelling at the time, Chen was transferred to area commander of Xi prefecture to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jingang seized Fen prefecture and many Jié-Xiongnu groups were in revolt, Chen was transferred to area commander of Xi prefecture to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 馭眾寬簡，夷夏安之。

translations.literal: He governed his troops with leniency and simplicity; both barbarians and Chinese lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and restraint, and both barbarians and Chinese lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 620.

sentences.zh: 子儉嗣，後隨例降爵為公。

translations.literal: His son Jian succeeded; later by precedent his title was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian succeeded him. Later, by precedent, his title was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 琛弟 孝恭河間王孝恭，琛之弟也。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Xiaogong — Prince of Hejian Xiaogong was Chen's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Xiaogong — Prince of Hejian Xiaogong was Chen's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京師，拜左光祿大夫，尋為山南道招慰大使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the capital, he was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; soon afterward he became commissioner for pacification of the South Mountain circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the capital, Xiaogong was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. Soon afterward he became commissioner for pacification of the South Mountain circuit.

sentences.zh: 自金州出於巴蜀，招攜以禮，降附者三十餘州。

translations.literal: From Jin prefecture he proceeded into Ba-Shu, winning people over with courtesy; more than thirty prefectures submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Setting out from Jin prefecture into Ba and Shu, he won people over with courtesy, and more than thirty prefectures submitted.

sentences.zh: 孝恭進擊硃粲，破之，諸將曰：「此食人賊也，為害實深，請坑之。」

translations.literal: Xiaogong pressed the attack on Zhu Can and defeated him; the generals said: "These are man-eating bandits; the harm they do runs very deep — please execute them by burying alive.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong pressed the attack on Zhu Can and defeated him. The generals said, "These are man-eating bandits who have done terrible harm. We ask that they be buried alive.

sentences.zh: 孝恭曰：「不可！

translations.literal: Xiaogong said: "You must not!
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong said, "No!

sentences.zh: 自此已東，皆為寇境，若聞此事，豈有來降者乎？」

translations.literal: From here eastward all lies within bandit territory — if they hear of this, will there be any who come to surrender?"
translations.idiomatic: From here eastward all is enemy territory. If word of this spreads, who will dare to surrender?

sentences.zh: 盡赦而不殺，由是書檄所至，相繼降款。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all and did not kill them; thereafter wherever his proclamations reached, submissions followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned them all instead. Thereafter, wherever his proclamations reached, surrender followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，授信州總管，承製拜假。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, he was appointed area commander of Xin prefecture with authority to grant provisional commissions by imperial writ.
translations.idiomatic: In 619 he was appointed area commander of Xin prefecture with authority to grant provisional commissions under imperial writ.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑據江陵，孝恭獻平銑之策，高祖嘉納之。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian held Jiangling; Xiaogong submitted a plan to pacify Xian, and Emperor Gaozu praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Xian held Jiangling, Xiaogong submitted a plan to defeat him, and Emperor Gaozu praised and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 三年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the third year his enfeoffment was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 620 his title was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 改信州為夔州，使拜孝恭為總管，令大造舟楫，教習水戰，以圖蕭銑。

translations.literal: Xin prefecture was renamed Kui prefecture; Xiaogong was appointed its area commander, ordered to build ships in great numbers and drill naval warfare, with the aim of taking Xiao Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xin prefecture was renamed Kui prefecture, and Xiaogong was appointed area commander there. He was ordered to build a large fleet and train his forces in naval warfare for a campaign against Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 孝恭召巴蜀首領子弟，量才授用，致之左右，外示引擢，而實以為質也。

translations.literal: Xiaogong summoned the sons of tribal leaders in Ba-Shu, appointed them according to their talents and kept them at his side; outwardly this showed promotion, but in fact they served as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong summoned the sons of Ba-Shu tribal leaders, assigned them posts suited to their abilities, and kept them close at hand. Outwardly it looked like promotion; in fact they were hostages.

sentences.zh: 尋授荊湘道行軍總管，統水陸十二總管，發自硤州，進軍江陵。

translations.literal: Soon he was made campaign commander of the Jing-Xiang circuit, commanding twelve area commanders by land and water; setting out from Xia prefecture, he marched on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed campaign commander of the Jing-Xiang circuit, with twelve land and naval commanders under him. He set out from Xia prefecture and advanced on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 攻其水城，克之，所得船散於江中。

translations.literal: He attacked their water fort and took it; the captured ships he scattered on the river.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed their river fort and took it, then scattered the captured ships down the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「虜得賊船，當藉其用，何為棄之，無乃資賊耶？」

translations.literal: All the generals said: "Capturing the rebel ships, we ought to make use of them — why abandon them? Will this not supply the bandits?
translations.idiomatic: The generals objected: "We should put those rebel ships to use. Why cast them away? Aren't we just handing the enemy an advantage?

sentences.zh: 孝恭曰：「不然，蕭銑偽境，南極嶺外，東至洞庭。

translations.literal: Xiaogong said: "Not so. Xiao Xian's rebel territory extends south to beyond the mountain ranges and east to Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong replied, "Not at all. Xiao Xian's rebel territory runs south to the far side of the Nanling ranges and east to Dongting.

sentences.zh: 若攻城未拔，援兵復到，我則內外受敵，進退不可，雖有舟楫，何所用之？

translations.literal: If the siege is not won and relief troops arrive again, we will be attacked inside and out, unable to advance or retreat — even with ships, of what use would they be?
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to take the city and their reinforcements arrive, we'll be caught between enemies with no room to advance or retreat. Even with ships, what good would they do us?

sentences.zh: 今銑緣江州鎮忽見船舸亂下，必知銑敗，未敢進兵，來去覘伺，動淹旬月，用緩其救，克之必矣。」

translations.literal: Now if the garrisons along the river suddenly see vessels drifting down in disorder, they will surely know Xian is defeated, will not dare advance, and will come and go spying and watching, delaying a full month or more — thus delaying their relief; victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's riverside garrisons see boats drifting downstream in disorder, they'll know he's lost and hesitate to advance. They'll linger on the river scouting for weeks—buying us time. Victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 銑救兵至巴陵，見船被江而下，果狐疑不敢輕進。

translations.literal: Xian's relief troops reached Baling; seeing ships spread across the river drifting downstream, they indeed grew suspicious and did not dare advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's relief force reached Baling, saw the scattered vessels floating downriver, and as Xiaogong had predicted, hung back in suspicion rather than press forward.

sentences.zh: 既內外阻絕，銑於是出降。

translations.literal: With communications inside and out cut off, Xian thereupon came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off both within and without, Xian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，拜孝恭荊州大總管，使畫工貌而視之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and appointed Xiaogong Grand Area Commander of Jing prefecture, having painters portray him for viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was delighted. He appointed Xiaogong Grand Area Commander of Jing prefecture and had painters render his likeness for the court to admire.

sentences.zh: 於是開置屯田，創立銅冶，百姓利焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened military colonies and established copper smelting; the common people benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He then established military colonies and copper works, to the benefit of the local populace.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷襄州道行台尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Left Vice President of the Xiangzhou Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: In 623 he was made Left Vice President of the Xiangzhou Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 時荊襄雖定，嶺表尚未悉平。

translations.literal: At the time although Jing-Xiang was settled, the region south of the ranges was not yet fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jing and Xiang were now secure, the far south had not yet been fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 孝恭分遣使人撫慰，嶺南四十九州皆來款附。

translations.literal: Xiaogong sent envoys in separate directions to soothe and reassure; all forty-nine prefectures south of the ranges came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong dispatched envoys throughout the region to win hearts and minds. All forty-nine prefectures south of the Nanling submitted.

sentences.zh: 及輔公祏據江東反，發兵寇壽陽，命孝恭為行軍元帥以擊之。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi held Jiangdong in rebellion, raised troops and raided Shouyang, Xiaogong was ordered as campaign commander to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi seized Jiangdong and rebelled, sending raiders against Shouyang, Xiaogong was appointed supreme campaign commander to crush him.

sentences.zh: 七年，孝恭自荊州趣九江，時李靖、李勣、黃君漢、張鎮州、盧祖尚並受孝恭節度。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Xiaogong advanced from Jing prefecture toward Jiujiang; at that time Li Jing, Li Ji, Huang Junhan, Zhang Zhenzhou, and Lu Zushang all fell under Xiaogong's command.
translations.idiomatic: In 624 Xiaogong marched from Jing prefecture toward Jiujiang. Li Jing, Li Ji, Huang Junhan, Zhang Zhenzhou, and Lu Zushang all served under his command.

sentences.zh: 將發，與諸將宴集，命取水，忽變為血，在座者皆失色。

translations.literal: Just before setting out, at a banquet with the generals he ordered water brought; it suddenly turned to blood, and all present changed color.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he banqueted his generals. When water was brought to the table it turned to blood. Every man present blanched.

sentences.zh: 孝恭舉止自若，徐諭之曰：「禍福無門，唯人所召。

translations.literal: Xiaogong carried himself as usual and slowly told them: "Fortune and disaster have no fixed door — only what men summon.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong remained composed. "Fortune and disaster have no fixed gate," he told them calmly. "They are only what men bring upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 自顧無負於物，諸公何見憂之深！

translations.literal: Considering myself, I have done nothing to wrong others — why do you gentlemen worry so deeply!
translations.idiomatic: I know I have wronged no one. Why are you so troubled?

sentences.zh: 公祏惡積禍盈，今承廟算以致討，碗中之血，乃公祏授首之後征。」

translations.literal: Gongshi's evil is piled up and his doom full; now we carry out the imperial plan to punish him — the blood in the bowl is an omen that Gongshi will lose his head after the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi has piled up evil until disaster must fall. We march under the emperor's plan to destroy him. This blood in the bowl is an omen that Gongshi will lose his head when the campaign ends.

sentences.zh: 遂盡飲而罷。

translations.literal: Then he drank it all and ended the feast.
translations.idiomatic: He drained the cup and dismissed the gathering.

sentences.zh: 時人服其識度而能安眾。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his insight and composure in settling the troops.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it marveled at his poise and his ability to steady the troops.

sentences.zh: 公祏遣其偽將馮惠亮、陳當時領水軍屯於博望山，陳正通、徐紹宗率步騎軍於青林山。

translations.literal: Gongshi sent his rebel generals Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi to lead the navy and encamp on Bowang Mountain; Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong led infantry and cavalry at Qinglin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi posted his generals Feng Huiliang and Chen Dangshi with the fleet on Bowang Mountain, and Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with infantry and cavalry on Qinglin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 孝恭至，堅壁不與斗，使奇兵斷其糧道。

translations.literal: When Xiaogong arrived, he strengthened his walls and would not give battle, sending surprise troops to cut off their supply routes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong arrived and refused battle behind strengthened defenses while detachments severed the rebel supply lines.

sentences.zh: 賊漸餧，夜薄我營，孝恭安臥不動。

translations.literal: The rebels grew gradually hungrier; by night they drew near our camp, but Xiaogong lay calmly without moving.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels grew hungrier, they raided the camp by night. Xiaogong slept on undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 明日，縱羸兵以攻賊壘，使盧祖尚率精騎列陣以待之。

translations.literal: The next day he sent weak troops to attack the rebel fort, while having Lu Zushang lead elite cavalry drawn up in formation to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent weak troops to feint at the rebel fort while Lu Zushang waited with elite cavalry in formation.

sentences.zh: 俄而攻壘者敗走，賊出追奔數里，遇祖尚軍，與戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Before long the attackers on the fort fled in defeat; the rebels came out in pursuit for several li, met Zushang's army, joined battle, and were routed.
translations.idiomatic: The feinting force broke and fled. The rebels gave chase for several li, ran into Lu Zushang's cavalry, and were routed.

sentences.zh: 正通棄營而走，復與馮惠亮保梁山。

translations.literal: Zhengtong abandoned his camp and fled, joining Feng Huiliang again to hold Liang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong abandoned his camp and rejoined Feng Huiliang on Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 孝恭乘勝攻之，破其梁山別鎮，赴水死者數千人，正通率陸軍夜遁。

translations.literal: Xiaogong pressed the victory and attacked, breaking their separate fort at Liang Mountain; several thousand drowned in the water; Zhengtong led the land army in flight by night.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong pressed the attack, stormed the secondary fort on Liang Mountain, and killed several thousand rebels who drowned trying to escape. Zhengtong fled by night with the land forces.

sentences.zh: 總管李靖又下廣陵城，拔楊子鎮。

translations.literal: Area Commander Li Jing also took Guangling city and captured Yangzi garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, area commander under Xiaogong, took Guangling and captured Yangzi garrison.

sentences.zh: 公祏窮蹙，棄丹陽東走。

translations.literal: Gongshi, hard pressed, abandoned Danyang and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Gongshi abandoned Danyang and fled east.

sentences.zh: 孝恭命騎將追之，至武康，擒公祏及其偽僕射西門君儀等數十人，致於麾下，江南悉平。
