translations.literal: Xiaogong ordered cavalry to pursue; at Wukang they captured Gongshi and his rebel Secretariat Director Ximen Junyi and several dozen others, bringing them under command; all of Jiangnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong sent cavalry in pursuit. At Wukang they captured Gongshi, his chancellor Ximen Junyi, and dozens of other rebels. Jiangnan was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒賞，賜甲第一區、女樂二部、奴婢七百人、金寶珍玩甚眾，授東南道行台尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: An imperial writ praised and rewarded him, granting one first-rank mansion, two troupes of singing girls, seven hundred servants, many gold treasures and precious curios, and appointing him Left Vice President of the Southeast Circuit Executive.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a commendatory decree, granting him a mansion of the first rank, two companies of female performers, seven hundred servants, and a profusion of gold, jewels, and treasures. He was appointed Left Vice President of the Southeast Circuit Executive.

sentences.zh: 後廢行台，拜揚州大都督。

translations.literal: Later the circuit executive was abolished and he was appointed Metropolitan Commissioner of Yang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit executive was later abolished, and he was appointed Metropolitan Commissioner of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝恭既破公祏，江淮及嶺南皆統攝之。

translations.literal: After Xiaogong had defeated Gongshi, he governed and controlled both Jiang-Huai and Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Gongshi, Xiaogong held authority over both the Jiang-Huai region and Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 自大業末，群雄競起，皆為太宗所平，謀臣猛將並在麾下，罕有別立勳庸者，唯孝恭著方面之功，聲名甚盛。

translations.literal: From the end of the Daye era competing warlords rose one after another, all pacified by Emperor Taizong; strategists and fierce generals were all under his banner — rarely did anyone else establish separate achievements; only Xiaogong achieved merit as a regional commander, his fame very great.
translations.idiomatic: From the chaos at the end of the Sui, one warlord after another had risen, and all were brought down by Emperor Taizong with his strategists and generals at his side. Few outside that inner circle won independent renown. Only Xiaogong earned distinction commanding a whole region, and his fame was immense.

sentences.zh: 厚自崇重，欲以威名鎮遠，築宅於石頭，陳廬徼以自衛。

translations.literal: He greatly exalted himself, wishing to hold the distant regions by renown alone; he built a mansion at Shitou and deployed fortified outposts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: He began to comport himself with growing grandeur, hoping his reputation alone would keep the frontier calm. He built an imposing estate at Shitou and posted fortified watch stations around it.

sentences.zh: 尋征拜宗正卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled and appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to court and appointed Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 九年，賜實封一千二百戶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was granted twelve hundred taxable households as substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In 626 he received an income of twelve hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，遷禮部尚書，以功臣封河間郡王，除觀州刺史，與長孫無忌等代襲刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of Rites; as a meritorious subject he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian commandery, dismissed to serve as prefect of Guan, and with Zhangsun Wuji and others alternated in succession as regional governors.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era he became Minister of Rites and, as a founding merit holder, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian. He was assigned as prefect of Guan and, together with Zhangsun Wuji and others, entered the rotation by which founding ministers served as regional governors.

sentences.zh: 孝恭性奢豪，重遊宴，歌姬舞女百有餘人，然而寬恕退讓，無驕矜自伐之色。

translations.literal: Xiaogong was by nature extravagant and proud, valuing feasts and entertainment; he had more than a hundred singing girls and dancing women — yet he was forgiving and yielding, with no arrogant or self-praising air.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong was extravagant by nature and devoted to feasting and entertainment. He kept more than a hundred singing girls and dancers. Yet he was forgiving and unassuming, without a trace of arrogance or self-congratulation.

sentences.zh: 太宗甚加親待，諸宗室中莫與為比。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong treated him with exceptional intimacy; among the imperial clan none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong treated him with exceptional favor. Among the imperial clan, none stood as close.

sentences.zh: 孝恭嘗悵然謂所親曰：「吾所居宅微為宏壯，非吾心也，當賣之，別營一所，粗令充事而已。

translations.literal: Xiaogong once said wistfully to those close to him: "The residence I dwell in is somewhat too grand — not to my liking. I should sell it and build another, merely sufficient for my needs.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong once told his intimates, with evident regret, "My house has grown a little too grand for my taste. I should sell it and build something modest—just enough to live in.

sentences.zh: 身歿之後。

translations.literal: After my death,
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone,

sentences.zh: 諸子若才，守此足矣；

translations.literal: if my sons have talent, keeping this will be enough;
translations.idiomatic: if my sons are capable, that will be enough for them;

sentences.zh: 如其不才，冀免他人所利也。」

translations.literal: if they lack talent, I hope to spare them from becoming others' prey."
translations.idiomatic: if they are not, I hope at least to keep others from coveting what I leave behind.

sentences.zh: 十四年，暴薨，年五十。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died suddenly, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly in 640, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 太宗素服舉哀，哭之甚慟，贈司空、揚州都督，陪葬獻陵，謚曰元，配享高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong wore plain mourning and raised laments, weeping with deep grief; posthumously appointed him Minister of Works and commissioner of Yang prefecture, buried with Xian mausoleum; posthumous title Yuan, given a place in Emperor Gaozu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong wore plain mourning and wept bitterly. Xiaogong was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and commissioner of Yangzhou, buried with Emperor Gaozu's Xian mausoleum, given the posthumous name Yuan, and granted a place in Emperor Gaozu's temple.

sentences.zh: 子崇義嗣，降爵為譙國公，歷蒲、同二州刺史，益州大都督長史，甚有威名。

translations.literal: His son Chongyi succeeded; his rank was reduced to Duke of Qiao state; he served in turn as prefect of Pu and Tong, chief administrator of the Yizhou Metropolitan Commission, and enjoyed great renown.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongyi succeeded him. His title was reduced to Duke of Qiao. He served as prefect of Pu and Tong in turn, then as chief administrator under the Yizhou Metropolitan Commissioner, and earned a formidable reputation.

sentences.zh: 後卒於宗正卿。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 孝恭次子晦，乾封中，累除營州都督，以善政聞；

translations.literal: Xiaogong's second son Hui, during Qianfeng, rose through successive removals to commissioner of Ying prefecture, known for good governance;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong's second son Hui, during the Qianfeng era, rose through successive appointments to commissioner of Ying prefecture, where his good governance became known;

sentences.zh: 璽書勞問，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: an imperial writ commended and inquired after him, granting three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a commendatory decree and three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 轉右金吾將軍，兼檢校雍州長史，糾發奸豪，無所容貸，為人吏畏服。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Golden Guard, concurrently acting chief administrator of Yong prefecture; he exposed and prosecuted powerful wrongdoers without leniency, and officials and commoners alike feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Right Golden Guard and concurrently made acting chief administrator of Yong prefecture. He prosecuted powerful wrongdoers without mercy, and officials and commoners alike feared and respected him.

sentences.zh: 晦私第有樓，下臨酒肆，其人嘗候晦言曰：「微賤之人，雖則禮所不及，然家有長幼，不欲外人窺之。

translations.literal: Hui's private residence had a tower overlooking a wineshop; the man once waited on Hui and said: "A man humble and low, though etiquette may not reach him, yet has elders and juniors in the family and does not wish outsiders to peep in.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's residence had a tower that looked down on a wineshop. The proprietor once came to him and said, "I am a humble man, scarcely worth your notice, but my household has elders and children, and we do not want strangers peering in on us.

sentences.zh: 家迫明公之樓，出入非便，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: My home presses against your lordship's tower — coming and going is inconvenient; I ask to take my leave from here."
translations.idiomatic: Your tower looms over my shop and makes coming and going difficult. I must ask to move elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 晦即日毀其樓。

translations.literal: That same day Hui had the tower demolished.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had the tower torn down that very day.

sentences.zh: 高宗將幸洛陽，令在京居守，顧謂之曰：「關中之事，一以付卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was about to visit Luoyang, he left Hui to guard the capital and turned to tell him: "Matters of Guanzhong — I entrust them entirely to you.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong prepared to travel to Luoyang, he left Hui in charge of the capital. "I entrust all affairs of Guanzhong to you," he told him.

sentences.zh: 但令式跼人，不可以成官政，令式之外，有利於人者，隨事即行，不須聞奏。」

translations.literal: Regulations alone constrain men and cannot by themselves make good government; beyond the regulations, wherever something benefits the people, carry it out as the occasion requires — no need to report for approval."
translations.idiomatic: Statutes alone cannot make good government. Wherever something outside the statutes would benefit the people, do it at once—no need to seek approval.

sentences.zh: 晦累有異績。

translations.literal: Hui repeatedly achieved outstanding results.
translations.idiomatic: Hui distinguished himself again and again.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu held court, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed power, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，拜右金吾衛大將軍，轉秋官尚書。

translations.literal: Early in Chuigong he was appointed General of the Right Golden Guard Regiment, then transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chuigong era he became General of the Right Golden Guard Regiment, then Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年卒，贈幽州都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang he died; posthumously appointed commissioner of You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 689 and was posthumously appointed commissioner of You prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子榮，為酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: His son Rong was killed by harsh investigators.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong was executed by the era's notorious harsh investigators.

sentences.zh: 琛弟 瑊孝恭弟瑊，武德中，為尚書右丞，封濟北郡王，卒於始州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Jian — Xiaogong's younger brother Jian, during Wude, served as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jibei commandery, and died as prefect of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Jian — Xiaogong's brother Jian — served during Wude as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. He was enfeoffed as Prince of Jibei and died while serving as prefect of Shi.

sentences.zh: 琛弟 瑰瑊弟瑰，義師克京城，授瑰左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Gui — Jian's younger brother Gui; when the righteous army took the capital, Gui was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Gui — when the Tang army took the capital, Gui was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，封漢陽郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 he was enfeoffed as Duke of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his enfeoffment was advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 622 his title was advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為侵寇，高祖使瑰齎布帛數萬段與結和親。

translations.literal: At the time the Turks repeatedly raided in invasion; Emperor Gaozu sent Gui bearing tens of thousands of bolts of silk to negotiate a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: As the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier, Emperor Gaozu sent Gui with tens of thousands of bolts of silk to negotiate a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗初見瑰，箕踞；

translations.literal: Il Khan at first meeting Gui sat spread-legged;
translations.idiomatic: When Il Khan first received Gui, he sat with legs sprawled in contempt;

sentences.zh: 瑰餌以厚利，頡利大悅，改容加敬，遣使隨瑰獻名馬。

translations.literal: Gui baited him with rich benefits; Il Khan was greatly pleased, changed his manner and showed respect, and sent an envoy with Gui to present famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gui won him over with lavish gifts. Il Khan was delighted, changed his manner, and sent an envoy back with Gui bearing fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 後復將命，頡利謂左右曰：「李瑰前來，恨不屈之，今者必令下拜。」

translations.literal: Later when he went on mission again, Il Khan told those beside him: "When Li Gui came before, I regretted not making him bow — this time I shall make him prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui returned on a later mission, Il Khan told his attendants, "Last time Li Gui came I regret not forcing him to bow. This time I will make him kowtow.

sentences.zh: 瑰微知之，及見頡利，長揖不屈節。

translations.literal: Gui subtly learned of this; when he met Il Khan, he gave a deep bow standing but would not bend in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Gui learned of the plan. When he met Il Khan he offered a deep bow but refused to kneel.

sentences.zh: 頡利大怒，乃留瑰不遣。

translations.literal: Il Khan was greatly angered and detained Gui, not sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: Il Khan was furious and detained him.

sentences.zh: 瑰神意自若，竟不為之屈。

translations.literal: Gui's spirit and bearing remained calm; in the end he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Gui remained calm throughout and never yielded.

sentences.zh: 頡利知不可以威脅，終禮遣之。

translations.literal: Il Khan knew he could not be cowed by threats and in the end sent him away with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that threats would not break him, Il Khan finally released him with proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 拜左武候將軍，轉衛尉卿，代兄孝恭為荊州都督。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard, transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and replaced his elder brother Xiaogong as commissioner of Jing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Left Martial Guard, then Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, succeeding his elder brother Xiaogong as commissioner of Jing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 政存清靜，深為士庶所懷。

translations.literal: His governance preserved clarity and tranquility; scholars and commoners deeply cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was quiet and fair, and scholars and commoners deeply trusted him.

sentences.zh: 嶺外豪帥屢相攻擊，遣使喻以威德，皆相次歸附，嶺表遂定。

translations.literal: Powerful chieftains beyond the ranges repeatedly attacked one another; he sent envoys to instruct them in imperial might and virtue, and all in succession submitted; the region south of the ranges was thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: When rival chieftains beyond the Nanling attacked one another, he sent envoys to instruct them in the empire's power and its mercy. They submitted one after another, and the far south was pacified.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，例降爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, by precedent his rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong came to the throne, Gui's title was reduced to duke by precedent.

sentences.zh: 時長史馮長命曾為御史大夫，素矜衒，事多專決，瑰怒杖之，坐是免。

translations.literal: At the time Chief Administrator Feng Changming had once been Censor-in-Chief, was by nature arrogant and showy, and decided many matters on his own; Gui in anger had him beaten with the staff and for this was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His chief administrator Feng Changming, a former Censor-in-Chief who was habitually arrogant, made many decisions on his own. Gui had him beaten for it and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，拜宜川刺史，加散騎常侍，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was appointed prefect of Yichuan, with additional title as Regular Attendant, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 630 he was appointed prefect of Yichuan with the additional title Regular Attendant, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子沖玄，垂拱中官至冬官尚書；

translations.literal: His son Chongxuan, during Chuigong, reached the office of Minister of Public Works;
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongxuan rose to Minister of Public Works during the Chuigong era;

sentences.zh: 沖虛，卒於尚方監。

translations.literal: Chongxu died while serving as Supervisor of the Imperial Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxu died while serving as Supervisor of the Imperial Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 廬江王瑗廬江王瑗，高祖從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Lujiang Yuan — Prince of Lujiang Yuan was a son of Emperor Gaozu's father's brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lujiang Yuan — Yuan was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu on the paternal line.

sentences.zh: 父哲，隋柱國、備身將軍，追封濟南王。

translations.literal: His father Zhe, Sui Pillar of State and Palace Guard General, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhe, a Sui Pillar of State and Palace Guard General, was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 瑗，武德元年曆信州總管，封廬江王。

translations.literal: Yuan, in the first year of Wude, served in turn as area commander of Xin prefecture and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 Yuan served as area commander of Xin prefecture and was enfeoffed as Prince of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 九年，累遷幽州大都督。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he rose through successive promotions to Metropolitan Commissioner of You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 626 he was promoted to Metropolitan Commissioner of You prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以瑗懦曌，非邊將才，遣右領軍將軍王君廓助典兵事。

translations.literal: The court considered Yuan weak and timid, not a frontier general's material, and sent Right Vanguard General Wang Junke to assist in managing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court judged Yuan too timid for a frontier command and sent Right Vanguard General Wang Junke to assist with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 君廓故嘗為盜，勇力絕人，瑗倚仗之，許結婚姻，以布心腹。

translations.literal: Junke had formerly been a bandit, with strength surpassing other men; Yuan relied on him, promised a marriage alliance, and used him to sound out trusted men.
translations.idiomatic: Junke had once been a bandit and possessed extraordinary strength. Yuan leaned on him, promised him a marriage alliance, and confided in him as a trusted intimate.

sentences.zh: 時隱太子建成將有異圖，外結於瑗。

translations.literal: At the time the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng was plotting treason and formed external ties with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince Jiancheng was plotting rebellion and cultivated ties with Yuan on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及建成誅死，遣通事舍人崔敦禮召瑗入朝，瑗有懼色。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng was executed, an Attendant in the Communications Office Cui Dunli was sent to summon Yuan to court; Yuan showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiancheng was executed, the palace envoy Cui Dunli was sent to summon Yuan to court. Yuan's fear showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 君廓素險薄，欲因事陷之以為己功，遂紿瑗曰：「京都有變，事未可知。

translations.literal: Junke was by nature treacherous and shallow, wishing to trap Yuan in an affair for his own credit; he then deceived Yuan, saying: "The capital has an upheaval — the matter is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: Junke, who was treacherous by nature, saw a chance to trap Yuan and claim the credit. He deceived Yuan: "There has been trouble in the capital—the outcome is still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 大王國之懿親，受委作鎮，寧得擁兵數萬而從一使召耶！

translations.literal: Great Prince, the state's honored kin, entrusted to hold a command — how can you hold tens of thousands of troops and obey a single envoy's summons!
translations.idiomatic: You are the emperor's own cousin, entrusted with a frontier army. How can you march to court at the word of one messenger while tens of thousands of soldiers stand at your back?

sentences.zh: 且聞趙郡王先以被拘，太子、齊王又言若此，大王今去，能自保乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover I hear Prince of Zhao was first detained, and with the crown prince and Prince of Qi speaking thus, if the great prince goes now, can you protect yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear Prince of Zhao has already been seized, and with things said to have gone against the crown prince and Prince of Qi alike—if you go now, can you be sure of your safety?

sentences.zh: 相與共泣。

translations.literal: They wept together.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together.

sentences.zh: 瑗乃囚敦禮，舉兵反。

translations.literal: Yuan then imprisoned Dunli and raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan imprisoned Dunli and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 召北齊州刺史王詵，將與計事，兵曹參軍王利涉說瑗曰：「王不奉詔而擅發兵，此為反矣。

translations.literal: He summoned Beiji prefecture magistrate Wang Shen to consult on plans; Army Staff Officer Wang Lishe admonished Yuan, saying: "Your Highness did not obey the edict but raised troops on your own — this is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Wang Shen, prefect of Beiji, to discuss strategy. Army Staff Officer Wang Lishe urged Yuan, "Your Highness has raised troops without imperial orders—that is rebellion.

sentences.zh: 須改易法度，以權宜應變，先定眾心。

translations.literal: You must change institutions and laws, adapt expediently to circumstances, and first settle the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: You must change your methods of rule, adapt as circumstances demand, and first win the hearts of your followers.

sentences.zh: 今諸州刺史或有逆命，王徵兵不集，何以保全？」

translations.literal: Now the various prefecture governors may refuse orders; if Your Highness summons troops and they do not assemble, how can you preserve yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: If the prefects refuse your orders and troops fail to rally when you call them, how will you protect yourself?

sentences.zh: 瑗曰：「若之何？」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan asked, "What then should we do?

sentences.zh: 利涉曰：「山東之地，先從竇建德，酋豪首領，皆是偽官，今並黜之，退居匹庶，此人思亂，若旱苗之望雨。

translations.literal: Lishe said: "The lands east of the mountains originally followed Dou Jiande; the tribal chiefs and leaders were all officials of the rebel regime, and now have all been dismissed and reduced to commoners. These people yearn for chaos like drought-stricken seedlings awaiting rain.
translations.idiomatic: Lishe replied, "East of the mountains once followed Dou Jiande. The tribal chiefs and local leaders were all officers of the rebel regime, but they have been dismissed and reduced to commoners. They hunger for rebellion like drought-blasted crops thirsting for rain.

sentences.zh: 王宜發使復其舊職，各於所在遣募本兵，諸州倘有不從，即委隨便誅戮。

translations.literal: Your Highness should send envoys to restore them to their former posts, and at each locality dispatch men to recruit their original troops; if any prefecture should not obey, then authorize execution as you see fit.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to restore them to their old offices and have them recruit their former followers locally. Wherever a prefecture refuses, authorize whoever is on the spot to execute the offenders.

sentences.zh: 此計若行，河北之地可呼吸而定也。

translations.literal: If this plan is carried out, the lands north of the Yellow River can be settled in the time it takes to draw one breath.
translations.idiomatic: If you adopt this plan, you can take Hebei as easily as drawing a breath.

sentences.zh: 然後分遣王詵北連突厥，道自太原，南臨蒲、絳；

translations.literal: Then separately dispatch Wang Shen north to join with the Turks, with the route from Taiyuan southward overlooking Pu and Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: Then send Wang Shen north to link up with the Turks, advancing from Taiyuan south toward Pu and Jiang;

sentences.zh: 大王整駕親詣洛陽，西入潼關。

translations.literal: the great prince should ready his chariot and go in person to Luoyang, entering Tong Pass from the west.
translations.idiomatic: while Your Highness yourself march on Luoyang and enter Tong Pass from the west.

sentences.zh: 兩軍合勢，不盈旬月，天下定矣。」

translations.literal: When the two armies combine strength, within less than ten days and a month the realm will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: With both armies united, the empire will be settled in less than a month.

sentences.zh: 瑗從之。

translations.literal: Yuan followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 瑗以內外機悉付君廓。

translations.literal: Yuan entrusted all internal and external affairs entirely to Junke.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan put all civil and military affairs entirely in Junke's hands.

sentences.zh: 利涉以君廓多翻覆，又說瑗委兵於王詵而除君廓，瑗不能決。

translations.literal: Lishe, because Junke was given to many turnabouts, again urged Yuan to entrust the army to Wang Shen and remove Junke; Yuan could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Lishe, distrusting Junke's unstable loyalty, urged Yuan to put the army under Wang Shen and remove Junke. Yuan could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 君廓知之，馳斬詵，持首告其眾曰：「李瑗與王詵共反，禁錮敕使，擅追兵集。

translations.literal: Junke learned of this, galloped and beheaded Shen, took the head and announced to the troops: "Li Yuan and Wang Shen rebel together, imprisoned the imperial envoy, and on their own authority summoned troops to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Junke learned of it, rode at speed, and killed Shen. Holding up the head, he told the troops, "Li Yuan has rebelled with Wang Shen. They imprisoned the imperial envoy and raised troops without authorization.

sentences.zh: 今王詵已斬，獨李瑗在，無能為也。

translations.literal: Now Wang Shen has already been beheaded; only Li Yuan remains — he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen is already dead. Only Yuan remains, and he can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 汝若從之，終亦族滅；

translations.literal: If you follow him, in the end your clans will also be exterminated;
translations.idiomatic: If you follow him, your families will be wiped out;

sentences.zh: 從我取之，立得富貴。

translations.literal: if you follow me to seize him, you will immediately gain wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: join me in seizing him and you will be rich and honored at once.

sentences.zh: 禍福如是，意欲何從？」

translations.literal: Ill fortune and good fortune are thus — what do you wish to follow?"
translations.idiomatic: Fortune or ruin lies before you— which will you choose?

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「皆願討賊。」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "We all wish to attack the traitor."
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers cried, "We will strike down the traitor.

sentences.zh: 君廓領其麾下登城西面，瑗未之覺。

translations.literal: Junke led his subordinates up the west face of the city wall; Yuan did not notice it.
translations.idiomatic: Junke led his men up the west wall of the city. Yuan did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 君廓自領千餘人先往獄中出敦禮，瑗始知之，遽率數百人披甲，才出至門外，與君廓相遇。

translations.literal: Junke himself led more than a thousand men first to the prison to release Dunli; Yuan then learned of it, hastily led several hundred men in armor, and had just gone out to the gate when he met Junke.
translations.idiomatic: Junke personally led more than a thousand men to the prison and freed Dunli. Yuan only then learned what was happening. He hastily mustered several hundred armored men and had scarcely stepped outside the gate when he ran into Junke.

sentences.zh: 君廓謂其眾曰：「李瑗作逆誤人，何忽從之，自取塗炭？」

translations.literal: Junke said to the crowd: "Li Yuan commits rebellion and misleads people — why suddenly follow him and seek your own ruin?"
translations.idiomatic: Junke shouted to Yuan's men, "Li Yuan led you into rebellion—why follow a traitor to your own destruction?

sentences.zh: 眾皆倒戈，一時潰走。

translations.literal: The crowd all turned their weapons around, and in an instant broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They turned their weapons on Yuan and fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 瑗塊然獨存，謂君廓曰：「小人賣我以自媚，汝行當自及矣。」

translations.literal: Yuan alone remained standing there; he said to Junke: "Petty men sold me out to curry favor — your turn will come soon enough."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan stood alone and said to Junke, "These petty men betrayed me to win your favor. Your own turn will come.

sentences.zh: 君廓擒瑗，縊殺之，年四十一，傳首京師，絕其屬籍。

translations.literal: Junke captured Yuan, strangled him to death; he was forty-one years old; his head was sent to the capital and his clan register was expunged.
translations.idiomatic: Junke seized Yuan and strangled him. Yuan was forty-one. His head was sent to the capital and his name was struck from the imperial clan rolls.

sentences.zh: 君廓，并州石艾人也。

translations.literal: Junke was a native of Shiai in Bing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Junke was a native of Shiai in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少亡命為群盜，聚徒千餘人，轉掠長平，進逼夏縣。

translations.literal: In youth he fled the law and became a bandit chief, gathered more than a thousand followers, roved and plundered Changping, and advanced to threaten Xia county.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he turned outlaw and became a bandit leader. He gathered more than a thousand followers, raided Changping, and pressed toward Xia County.

sentences.zh: 李密遣使召之，遂投於密。

translations.literal: Li Mi sent an envoy to summon him, and he thereupon submitted to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent for him, and he went over to Mi's side.

sentences.zh: 尋又率眾歸國，歷遷右武衛將軍，累封彭國公。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he also led the multitude to submit to the state, was promoted through successive steps to Right Martial Guard General, and repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led his followers to submit to Tang. He rose through successive posts to Right Martial Guard General and was enfeoffed repeatedly as Duke of Peng.

sentences.zh: 從平劉黑闥，令鎮幽州。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Liu Heita and was ordered to garrison You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After campaigning against Liu Heita, he was assigned to guard Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，君廓邀擊破之，俘斬二千餘人，獲馬五千匹。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided, Junke intercepted and defeated them, capturing and beheading more than two thousand men and obtaining five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided the frontier, Junke intercepted and routed them, killing or capturing more than two thousand men and taking five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，徵入朝，賜以御馬，令於殿庭乘之而出，因謂侍臣曰：「吾聞藺相如叱秦皇，目皆出血。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased, summoned him to court, bestowed an imperial horse, and had him mount and ride out in the palace courtyard; he then said to the attending ministers: "I have heard that when Lin Xiangru rebuked the King of Qin, blood came from his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was delighted. He summoned Junke to court, gave him an imperial horse, and had him ride it out across the palace courtyard. Then he told the ministers, "I have heard that when Lin Xiangru berated the King of Qin, blood burst from his eyes.

sentences.zh: 君廓往擊竇建德，將出戰，李靖遏之，君廓發憤大呼，目及鼻耳一時流血。

translations.literal: When Junke went to attack Dou Jiande and was about to go forth to battle, Li Jing held him back; Junke in fury cried out loudly, and from his eyes together with his nose and ears blood flowed all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Junke was about to ride out against Dou Jiande, Li Jing restrained him. Junke roared in fury until blood streamed from his eyes, nose, and ears at once.

sentences.zh: 此之壯氣，何謝古人，不可以常例賞之。」

translations.literal: Such bold spirit — what need to defer to the ancients? He cannot be rewarded by ordinary precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Such courage needs no apology to the ancients. He must be rewarded beyond ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 復賜錦袍金帶，還鎮幽州。

translations.literal: He again bestowed a brocade robe and gold belt, and sent him back to garrison You prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu granted him a brocade robe and gold belt and sent him back to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以誅瑗功，拜左領軍大將軍，兼幽州都督，以瑗家口賜之，加左光祿大夫，賜物千段，食實封千三百戶。

translations.literal: Soon for the merit of executing Yuan he was appointed Left Army General-in-Chief, concurrently Metropolitan Protector of You prefecture; Yuan's household was given to him; he received the additional title Left Grand Master of Splendorous Happiness, a gift of a thousand bolts of goods, and a fief income of thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Left Army General-in-Chief and concurrently Metropolitan Protector of Youzhou for killing Yuan. Gaozu gave him Yuan's household, added the title Left Grand Master of Splendorous Happiness, granted a thousand bolts of goods, and conferred a fief of thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 在職多縱逸，長史李玄道數以朝憲脅之，懼為所奏，殊不自安。

translations.literal: In office he was largely unrestrained; Chief Administrator Li Xuandao repeatedly threatened him with court law, and fearing he would be denounced, he was deeply ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was habitually unrestrained. Chief Administrator Li Xuandao repeatedly threatened him with imperial law. Fearing denunciation, he grew profoundly uneasy.

sentences.zh: 後追入朝，行至渭南，殺驛史而遁。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled to court; when he reached Weinan he killed the relay-station clerk and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled to court. At Weinan he killed the relay clerk and fled.

sentences.zh: 將奔突厥，為野人所殺，追削其封邑。

translations.literal: About to flee to the Turks, he was killed by wildfolk; his enfeoffment was posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: He was heading for the Turks when country folk killed him. His fief was posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王道玄淮陽王道玄，高祖從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan — Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan was a son of Emperor Gaozu's father's brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Huaiyang Daoxuan — Daoxuan was a cousin of Emperor Gaozu on the paternal line.

sentences.zh: 祖繪，隋夏州總管，武德初，追封雍王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui, Sui area commander of Xia prefecture, at the beginning of Wude was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had served as area commander of Xiazhou under the Sui. At the start of the Tang he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 父贄，追封河南王。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 道玄，武德元年封淮陽王，授右千牛。

translations.literal: Daoxuan, in the first year of Wude was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang and appointed to the Right Thousand-Ox guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 Daoxuan was enfeoffed Prince of Huaiyang and appointed to the Right Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊宋金剛於介州，先登陷陣，時年十五，太宗壯之，賞物千段。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Taizong in attacking Song Jingang at Jie prefecture, was first to ascend and break the enemy line; he was then fifteen years old; Emperor Taizong admired him and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he followed Taizong against Song Jingang at Jiezhou, was first over the ramparts and through the enemy line. Taizong was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 後從討王世充，頻戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Later he followed in campaigning against Wang Shichong; in repeated battles all were victories.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned against Wang Shichong and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 竇建德至武牢，太宗以輕騎誘賊，領道玄率伏兵於道左，會賊至，追擊破之。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande reached Hulao, Emperor Taizong used light cavalry to lure the enemy; leading Daoxuan he placed ambush troops on the left of the road; when the enemy arrived they pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande reached Hulao, Taizong used light cavalry as bait. Daoxuan led hidden troops along the left flank. When the enemy closed in, they were pursued and broken.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗轉戰於汜水，麾戈陷陣，直出賊後，眾披靡，復衝突而歸。

translations.literal: Again he followed Emperor Taizong in shifting battle to Sishui, waving his halberd breaking through the line, going straight out behind the enemy; the multitude was scattered and he charged back again.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui he fought under Taizong again, halberd in hand, smashing through the line, circling behind the enemy, scattering their ranks, and charging back through them.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，命副乘以給道玄。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and ordered a second chariot given to Daoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was delighted and gave Daoxuan a spare chariot of his own.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗赴賊，再入再出，飛矢亂下，箭如蝟毛，猛氣益厲，射人無不應弦而倒。

translations.literal: Again following Emperor Taizong charging the enemy, twice entering and twice exiting, flying arrows rained down chaotically, arrows like a hedgehog's bristles; his fierce spirit grew keener; those he shot all fell at the sound of the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Riding again with Taizong into the enemy, he entered and withdrew twice while arrows fell like rain and bristled like a hedgehog's quills. His fury only sharpened. Every man he shot fell at the twang of his bow.

sentences.zh: 東都平，拜洛州總管。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified, he was appointed area commander of Luo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was pacified, he was made area commander of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 及府廢，改授洛州刺史。

translations.literal: When the area command was abolished, he was changed to appointment as prefect of Luo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the area command was abolished, he was reassigned as prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，劉黑闥引突厥寇河北，復授山東道行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Liu Heita led the Turks to raid north of the Yellow River; he was again appointed Commander on Campaign of the Shandong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 622, when Liu Heita led Turks into Hebei, Daoxuan was again made Commander on Campaign of the Shandong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 師次下博，與賊軍遇，道玄帥騎先登，命副將史萬寶督軍繼進。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xiabo and encountered the rebel army; Daoxuan led cavalry in the van charge, ordering Deputy Commander Shi Wanbao to supervise the army in following advance.
translations.idiomatic: His army encamped at Xiabo, where it met the rebels. Daoxuan led the cavalry charge himself and ordered his deputy Shi Wanbao to bring up the main force.

sentences.zh: 萬寶與之不協，及道玄深入，而擁兵不進，謂所親曰：「吾奉手詔，言淮陽小兒雖名為將，而軍之進止皆委於吾。

translations.literal: Wanbao was at odds with him; when Daoxuan penetrated deeply, he held the troops and did not advance, saying to those close to him: "I received a handwritten edict saying that though the boy of Huaiyang is named general, the army's advance and halt are all entrusted to me.
translations.idiomatic: Wanbao resented him. When Daoxuan pressed deep into the enemy lines, Wanbao held the main force back. He told his intimates, "I carry a handwritten edict saying that although the Huaiyang boy bears the title of general, advance and halt are mine to decide.

sentences.zh: 今其輕脫，越濘交戰，大軍若動，必陷泥溺，莫如結陣以待之，雖不利於王，而利於國。」

translations.literal: Now his rashness crosses the mire to give battle; if the great army moves it will surely sink into mud and swamp — better to form battle lines and wait; though it may not benefit the prince, it will benefit the state."
translations.idiomatic: He is reckless—crossing marshland to fight. If we march the main force forward, we will bog down. Better to hold formation and wait. That may harm the prince, but it will serve the state.

sentences.zh: 道玄遂為賊所擒，全軍盡沒，惟萬寶逃歸。

translations.literal: Daoxuan was then captured by the enemy; the entire army was lost; only Wanbao escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan was taken by the enemy and his whole force wiped out. Only Wanbao escaped.

sentences.zh: 道玄遇害，年十九。

translations.literal: Daoxuan met with calamity; he was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan was killed. He was nineteen.

sentences.zh: 太宗追悼久之，嘗從容謂侍臣曰：「道玄終始從朕，見朕深入賊陣，所向必克，意嘗企慕，所以每陣先登，蓋學朕也。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong mourned him for a long time; once at leisure he said to the attending ministers: "Daoxuan followed me from beginning to end; seeing me penetrate deeply into the enemy lines and wherever I turned be victorious, his mind always aspired to this; therefore in every battle he charged first — he was learning from me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him for a long while. Once he told his ministers at ease, "Daoxuan followed me everywhere. He watched me plunge deep into enemy lines and win wherever I turned, and he wanted to be like me. That is why he charged first in every battle—he was learning from me.

sentences.zh: 惜其年少，不遂遠圖。」

translations.literal: It is a pity he was young and did not fulfill a distant design."
translations.idiomatic: It is a pity he was so young and never lived to achieve great things.

sentences.zh: 因為之流涕。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 贈左驍衛大將軍，謚曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Left Guard Cavalry General-in-Chief; posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Left Guard Cavalry General-in-Chief and given the posthumous name Zhuang, meaning Bold.

sentences.zh: 無子，詔封其弟武都郡公道明為淮陽王，令主道玄之祀。

translations.literal: Having no son, an edict enfeoffed his younger brother Commandery Duke of Wudu Daoming as Prince of Huaiyang, ordering him to preside over Daoxuan's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons. An edict enfeoffed his younger brother Daoming, Duke of Wudu, as Prince of Huaiyang to maintain Daoxuan's ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 累遷左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to Left Guard Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming rose through successive posts to Left Guard Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 送弘化公主還蕃，坐洩主非太宗女，奪爵國除，後卒於鄆州刺史。

translations.literal: Escorting Princess Honghua back to the foreign realm, he was punished for revealing that the princess was not Emperor Taizong's daughter; his title was stripped and the fief abolished; later he died while serving as prefect of Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting Princess Honghua back to her people he let slip that she was not Taizong's daughter. His title was stripped and his fief abolished. He later died as prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 道玄從父弟 道宗江夏王道宗，道玄從父弟也。

translations.literal: Daoxuan's father's younger brother's son — Daozong Prince of Jiangxia Daozong was Daoxuan's father's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Daoxuan's paternal cousin — Prince of Jiangxia Daozong was Daoxuan's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 父韶，追封東平王，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Shao was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping and given the posthumous gift title Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Dongping and given the posthumous title Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 道宗，武德元年封略陽郡公，起家左千牛備身。

translations.literal: Daozong, in the first year of Wude was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang commandery and began his career as Left Thousand-Ox guard attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 618 Daozong was enfeoffed Duke of Lueyang and entered service as Left Thousand-Ox Guard attendant.

sentences.zh: 討劉武周，戰於度索原，軍敗，賊徒進逼河東。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Liu Wuzhou, they fought at Dusuoyuan; the army was defeated and the rebel bands advanced pressing on Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Liu Wuzhou, he fought at Dusuoyuan. The Tang army was defeated and the rebels pressed toward Hedong.

sentences.zh: 道宗時年十七，從太宗率眾拒之。

translations.literal: Daozong was then seventeen years old; he followed Emperor Taizong leading the multitude to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong was seventeen. He followed Taizong in leading troops to resist them.

sentences.zh: 太宗登玉壁城望賊，顧謂道宗曰：「賊恃其眾來邀我戰，汝謂如何？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong ascended Yubi city to look at the enemy, turned and said to Daozong: "The enemy relying on their numbers comes inviting us to battle — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: From the walls of Yubi, Taizong surveyed the enemy and turned to Daozong. "They rely on numbers and want to force us into battle. What do you advise?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「群賊乘勝，其鋒不可當，易以計屈，難與力競。

translations.literal: He replied: "The band of rebels riding victory — their edge cannot be met; it is easy to subdue them with stratagem, hard to compete with them in force.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong answered, "They come flush with victory—their momentum cannot be met head on. They can be broken by stratagem, not by force.

sentences.zh: 今深壁高壘，以挫其鋒；

translations.literal: Now deeply wall and raise ramparts to blunt their edge;
translations.idiomatic: Fortify the walls and raise the ramparts to blunt their attack;

sentences.zh: 烏合之徒，莫能持久，糧運致竭，自當離散，可不戰而擒。」

translations.literal: a motley crowd cannot endure long; when grain transport is exhausted they will naturally scatter — they can be captured without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: a rabble like this cannot hold together. When their grain runs out they will break apart, and we can take them without fighting.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「汝意暗與我合。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "Your thought secretly agrees with mine."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Your counsel matches my own.

sentences.zh: 後賊果食盡夜遁，追及介州，一戰滅之。

translations.literal: Later the enemy indeed exhausted food and fled by night; pursued to Jie prefecture, they were destroyed in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did run out of supplies and fled by night. Taizong caught them at Jiezhou and destroyed them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 又從平竇建德，破王世充，屢有殊效。

translations.literal: Again he followed in pacifying Dou Jiande and defeating Wang Shichong, repeatedly having exceptional achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He later helped pacify Dou Jiande and defeat Wang Shichong and distinguished himself again and again.

sentences.zh: 五年，授靈州總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed area commander of Ling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 622 he was appointed area commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁師都據夏州，遣弟洛仁引突厥兵數萬至於城下。

translations.literal: Liang Shidou held Xia prefecture and sent his younger brother Luoren to lead tens of thousands of Turk troops to the foot of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidou held Xiazhou and sent his brother Luoren with tens of thousands of Turk horsemen to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 道宗閉門拒守，伺隙而戰，賊徒大敗。

translations.literal: Daozong closed the gates and refused to yield, waited for an opening to fight, and the rebel bands were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong shut the gates and held firm, then struck when he saw an opening and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉之，謂左僕射裴寂、中書令蕭瑀曰：「道宗今能守邊，以寡制眾。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard and commended it, saying to Left Vice Director Pei Ji and Central Secretariat Director Xiao Yu: "Daozong now can guard the frontier, using the few to control the many.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised the feat and told Vice Director Pei Ji and Central Secretariat Director Xiao Yu, "Daozong can now defend the frontier and defeat larger forces with smaller ones.

sentences.zh: 昔魏任城王彰臨戎卻敵，道宗勇敢，有同於彼。」

translations.literal: Formerly Wei Prince of Rencheng Zhang at the fore repelled the enemy; Daozong's bravery is the same as his."
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Prince Zhang of Rencheng drove back the enemy in person on the battlefield. Daozong's courage is the same.

sentences.zh: 遂封為任城王。

translations.literal: He was thereupon enfeoffed as Prince of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon enfeoffed Prince of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 初，突厥連於梁師都，其郁射設入居五原舊地，道宗逐出之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turks were allied with Liang Shidou; their Yushe she entered and occupied the old lands of Wuyuan; Daozong drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Turks had allied with Liang Shidou. Their chieftain Yushe settled in the old Wuyuan territory, and Daozong drove him out.

sentences.zh: 振耀威武，開拓疆界，斥地千餘里，邊人悅服。

translations.literal: Displaying martial might, he opened and expanded the frontier, pushing the border more than a thousand li; frontier people submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: He made a display of force, pushed the border more than a thousand li, and won over the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，征拜鴻臚卿，歷左領軍、大理卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonial; he passed through Left Army command and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 627 he was summoned to court as Minister of Ceremonial, later serving as Left Army commander and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時太宗將經略突厥，又拜靈州都督。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Taizong was about to plan operations against the Turks, and he was again appointed Metropolitan Protector of Ling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizong prepared campaigns against the Turks, Daozong was again made Metropolitan Protector of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，為大同道行軍總管。

translations.literal: In the third year he served as Commander on Campaign of the Datong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 629 he became Commander on Campaign of the Datong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 遇李靖襲破頡利可汗，頡利以十餘騎來奔其部。

translations.literal: When Li Jing in a surprise attack broke Jieli Khan, Jieli with more than ten horsemen came fleeing to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jing's surprise attack broke Jieli Khan, Jieli fled with a dozen horsemen toward Daozong's command.

sentences.zh: 道宗引兵逼之，征其執送頡利。

translations.literal: Daozong led troops pressing on them and demanded they seize and deliver Jieli.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong advanced and ordered the local tribes to seize Jieli and send him in.

sentences.zh: 頡利以數騎夜走，匿於荒谷，沙鈐羅懼，馳追獲之，遣使送於京師。

translations.literal: Jieli with several horsemen fled by night, hiding in a desolate valley; Shaqiluo in fear galloped in pursuit and captured him, sending an envoy to deliver him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli slipped away by night with a few riders and hid in a desolate valley. Shaqiluo, fearing reprisals, rode in pursuit, captured him, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功賜實封六百戶，召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: For the merit he was granted a fief income of six hundred households; he was summoned and appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: For this he received a fief of six hundred households and was made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾寇邊，詔右僕射李靖為昆丘道行軍大總管，道宗與吏部尚書侯君集為之副。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun raided the frontier; an edict appointed Right Vice Director Li Jing as Great Commander on Campaign of the Kunqiu Circuit; Daozong together with Minister of Civil Appointments Hou Junji served as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier, Li Jing was made Great Commander on the Kunqiu Circuit, with Daozong and Minister of Civil Appointments Hou Junji as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 賊聞兵至，走入嶂山，已行數千里。

translations.literal: The enemy hearing the army had arrived, entered Zhang mountain and had already marched several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the army approach, the enemy fled into the Zhang Mountains, already thousands of li away.

sentences.zh: 諸將議欲息兵，道宗固請追討，李靖然之，而君集不從。

translations.literal: The generals deliberated wishing to rest the army; Daozong firmly requested pursuit; Li Jing agreed, but Junji did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals wanted to halt the campaign. Daozong insisted on pursuit. Li Jing agreed, but Hou Junji refused.

sentences.zh: 道宗遂率偏師並行倍道，去大軍十日，追及之。

translations.literal: Daozong then led a detached division marching by parallel routes at double speed; ten days from the main army he caught up with them.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong led a detached column by forced marches on a parallel route and caught the enemy ten days ahead of the main army.

sentences.zh: 賊據險苦戰，道宗潛遣千餘騎逾山襲其後，賊表裡受敵，一時奔潰。

translations.literal: The enemy held perilous ground and fought bitterly; Daozong secretly sent more than a thousand cavalry crossing the mountain to strike their rear; the enemy suffered attack front and rear and at once broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fought from strong ground. Daozong secretly sent a thousand horsemen over the mountains to strike their rear. Caught between two forces, they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷禮部尚書，改封江夏王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites and his enfeoffment changed to Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In 638 he was transferred to Minister of Rites and enfeoffed Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 尋坐贓下獄。

translations.literal: Soon he sat for corruption and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was imprisoned on corruption charges.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「朕富有四海，士馬如林，欲使轍跡周宇內，遊觀無休息，絕域采奇玩，海外訪珍羞，豈不得耶？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said to the attending ministers: "I possess the four seas, soldiers and horses like a forest — if I wished to make wheel tracks circle the realm, tour and observe without rest, gather strange curios from distant lands, and seek rare delicacies from beyond the seas, could I not?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his ministers, "I possess the four seas and armies without number. If I wished to ride my chariot to every corner of the realm, tour without rest, gather rare curios from distant lands, and feast on delicacies from beyond the sea—could I not?

sentences.zh: 勞萬姓而樂一人，朕所不取也。

translations.literal: To weary the myriad people and delight one man — this I will not take.
translations.idiomatic: But I will not weary my people for my own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 人心無厭，唯當以理制之。

translations.literal: The people's hearts know no satiety; only by reason should this be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Human desire knows no limit. It must be held in check by principle.

sentences.zh: 道宗俸料甚高，宴賜不少，足有餘財，而貪婪如此，使人嗟惋，豈不鄙乎！」

translations.literal: Daozong's salary stipend is very high, banquet gifts are not few — he has ample surplus wealth — yet he is greedy thus; it makes one sigh in regret; is this not base!
translations.idiomatic: Daozong's salary is generous and his banquets plentiful. He has more than enough wealth, yet he grasped for more. It is lamentable—and contemptible!

sentences.zh: 遂免官，削封邑。

translations.literal: He was thereupon dismissed from office and his fief domain was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office and his fief was reduced.

sentences.zh: 十三年，起為茂州都督，未行，轉晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was recalled to serve as metropolitan protector of Mao prefecture; before departing he was transferred to prefect of Jin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 639 he was recalled as Metropolitan Protector of Maozhou. Before he could take up the post, he was transferred to prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 640 he was again appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時侯君集立功於高昌，自負其才，潛有異志。

translations.literal: At the time Hou Junji had achieved merit in Gaochang, prided himself on his talent, and secretly harbored divergent intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji had distinguished himself in the conquest of Gaochang. Confident in his abilities, he secretly harbored treacherous ambitions.

sentences.zh: 道宗嘗因侍宴，從容言曰：「君集智小言大，舉止不倫，以臣觀之，必為戎首。」

translations.literal: Daozong once at a banquet attendant, speaking at ease said: "Junji has small wisdom and big words, his conduct is irregular — in this subject's view he will surely become a rebel leader.
translations.idiomatic: At a court banquet Daozong said calmly, "Junji's wit is small but his talk is grand, and his behavior is unseemly. In my view, he will lead a rebellion.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「何以知之？」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "How do you know this?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked, "How can you tell?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「見其恃有微功，深懷矜伐，恥在房玄齡、李靖之下。

translations.literal: He replied: "Seeing that he relies on slight merit, deeply cherishes boasting of himself, and is ashamed to stand below Fang Xuanling and Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong answered, "He takes pride in modest achievements, boasts of them openly, and resents ranking below Fang Xuanling and Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 雖為吏部尚書，未滿其志，非毀時賢，常有不平之語。」

translations.literal: Although serving as Minister of Civil Appointments, his ambition is not fulfilled; he slanders men of the age and constantly has words of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as Minister of Civil Appointments his ambitions are unsatisfied. He speaks ill of worthy contemporaries and often voices bitter complaints.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「不可億度，浪生猜貳。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "One must not guess at such things and rashly breed suspicion and division.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "One must not speculate rashly and breed needless suspicion.

sentences.zh: 其功勳才用，無所不堪，朕豈惜重位？

translations.literal: His merit and talent are fit for anything — would I begrudge a high position?
translations.idiomatic: His achievements and talent qualify him for the highest posts. Would I stint on rank?

sentences.zh: 第未到耳。」

translations.literal: It is only that the time has not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The time simply has not come yet.

sentences.zh: 俄而君集謀反誅，太宗笑謂道宗曰：「君集之事，果如公所揣。」

translations.literal: Soon Junji plotted rebellion and was executed; Emperor Taizong smiling said to Daozong: "Junji's affair indeed turned out as you conjectured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hou Junji was executed for treason. Taizong smiled and told Daozong, "Junji's case proved exactly as you foresaw.

sentences.zh: 及大軍討高麗，令道宗與李靖為前鋒，濟遼水，克蓋牟城。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Goguryeo, Daozong and Li Jing were ordered as vanguard, crossed the Liao River, and captured Gaemu city.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched against Goguryeo, Daozong and Li Jing led the vanguard, crossed the Liao River, and took Gaemu City.

sentences.zh: 逢賊兵大至，軍中僉欲深溝保險，待太宗至徐進，道宗曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Meeting the enemy army arriving in force, in the army all wished to dig deep trenches and hold defensible ground, waiting for Emperor Taizong to arrive before advancing slowly; Daozong said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: When a large enemy force appeared, the officers all wanted to entrench and hold strong ground until Taizong arrived. Daozong said, "We cannot do that.

sentences.zh: 賊赴急遠來，兵實疲頓，恃眾輕我，一戰必摧。

translations.literal: The enemy hurrying from afar in urgency — their troops are truly exhausted; relying on their numbers they despise us — one battle will surely shatter them.
translations.idiomatic: They have marched far in haste and their troops are exhausted. They rely on numbers and underestimate us. One strike will break them.

sentences.zh: 昔耿弇不以賊遺君父，我既職在前軍，當須清道以待輿駕。」

translations.literal: Formerly Geng Yan did not leave the enemy for his lord and father; since I hold duty in the vanguard army, I must clear the road to await the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Yan refused to leave the enemy for his sovereign. As vanguard commander it is my duty to clear the way for the emperor's march.

sentences.zh: 李靖然之。

translations.literal: Li Jing assented.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃與壯士數十騎直衝賊陣，左右出入，靖因合擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Then with several dozen bold horsemen he charged straight into the enemy line, entering and exiting left and right; Jing thereupon combined attacks and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He took several dozen picked horsemen and charged straight into the enemy lines, wheeling in and out. Li Jing joined the attack and they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 太宗至，深加賞勞，賜奴婢四十人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong arrived he deeply added reward and consolation, bestowing forty slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong arrived he praised Daozong lavishly and granted him forty household slaves.

sentences.zh: 又築土山攻安市城，土山崩，道宗失於部署，為賊所據。

translations.literal: Again they built an earthen mound to attack Ancheng city; the earthen mound collapsed; Daozong failed in deployment and it was seized by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They also raised an earthen mound to assault Ancheng. The mound collapsed. Daozong's dispositions failed, and the enemy seized it.

sentences.zh: 歸罪於果毅傅伏愛，斬之。

translations.literal: He attributed guilt to the brave corps officer Fu Fu'ai and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed Brave Corps Officer Fu Fu'ai and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 道宗跣行詣旗下請罪，太宗曰：「漢武殺王恢，不如秦穆赦孟明，土山之失，且非其罪。」

translations.literal: Daozong barefoot went to the military banner to request punishment; Emperor Taizong said: "Emperor Wu of Han killed Wang Hui — it was not as good as Duke Mu of Qin pardoning Meng Ming; the loss of the earthen mound is moreover not his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong went barefoot to the command banner to accept punishment. Taizong said, "When Emperor Wu executed Wang Hui he acted less wisely than Duke Mu of Qin, who pardoned Meng Ming. The loss of the mound was not wholly your fault.

sentences.zh: 舍而不問。

translations.literal: He released it without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the matter without further punishment.

sentences.zh: 道宗在陣損足，太宗親為其針，賜以御膳。

translations.literal: Daozong in battle injured his foot; Emperor Taizong personally stitched it for him and bestowed imperial fare.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong was wounded in the foot during battle. Taizong personally stitched the wound and gave him food from the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以疾請居閒職，轉太常卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, citing illness he requested a leisurely post and was transferred to Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: In 647, citing illness, he asked for a less demanding post and was made Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，加授特進，增實封並前六百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he received the additional appointment of Special Advancement, with increased fief income bringing the total to six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In 650 he was given the honorific title Special Advance and his fief income was raised to six hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 四年，房遺愛伏誅，長孫無忌、褚遂良素與道宗不協，上言道宗與遺愛交結，配流象州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Fang Yiai was executed; Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang had long been at odds with Daozong; they memorialized that Daozong was linked with Yiai; he was sentenced to exile in Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 653, when Fang Yiai was executed, Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang—long at odds with Daozong—accused him of conspiring with Yiai. He was exiled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，年五十四。

translations.literal: En route he fell ill and died; he was fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the journey and died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 及無忌、遂良得罪，詔復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Wuji and Suiliang fell into guilt, an edict restored his office and titles.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuji and Suiliang themselves were condemned, an edict restored Daozong's ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 道宗晚年頗好學，敬慕賢士，不以地勢凌人，宗室中唯道宗及河間王孝恭昆季最為當代所重。

translations.literal: Daozong in his later years greatly loved learning, revered worthy scholars, and did not bully people by his lofty status; among the imperial clan only Daozong and the Prince of Hejian Xiaogong and his brothers were most honored by their generation.
translations.idiomatic: In later life Daozong devoted himself to learning, admired men of talent, and never bullied others with his rank. Among the imperial clan, he and Prince Xiaogong of Hejian and his brothers were the most respected men of their time.

sentences.zh: 道宗子景恆，降封盧國公，官至相州刺史。

translations.literal: Daozong's son Jingheng was reduced in enfeoffment to Duke of Lu, and reached the post of prefect of Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong's son Jingheng was demoted to Duke of Lu and rose to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 隴西王博乂隴西王博乂，高祖兄子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Longxi Boyi — Prince of Longxi Boyi was a son of Emperor Gaozu's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Boyi of Longxi — Boyi was Emperor Gaozu's nephew.

sentences.zh: 高祖長兄曰澄，次曰湛，次曰洪，並早卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu's eldest elder brother was called Cheng, the next Zhan, the next Hong — all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's elder brothers were, in order, Cheng, Zhan, and Hong. All died young.

sentences.zh: 武德初，追封澄為梁王，湛為蜀王，洪為鄭王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, Cheng was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, Zhan as Prince of Shu, Hong as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tang, Cheng was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Liang, Zhan Prince of Shu, and Hong Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 澄、洪並無後，博乂即湛第二子也。

translations.literal: Cheng and Hong both had no descendants; Boyi was Zhan's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Hong left no heirs. Boyi was Zhan's second son.

sentences.zh: 武德元年受封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He received his title in 618.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，歷宗正卿、禮部尚書，加特進。

translations.literal: During Emperor Gaozu's time he passed through Director of the Imperial Clan, Minister of Rites, and received Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he served as Director of the Imperial Clan and Minister of Rites and received the honorific Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 博乂有妓妾數百人，皆衣羅綺，食必粱肉，朝夕纟玄歌自娛，驕侈無比。

translations.literal: Boyi had several hundred courtesans and concubines, all clothed in silk gauze, eating only fine grain and meat, morning and evening singing with string music to amuse himself — arrogant extravagance without compare.
translations.idiomatic: Boyi kept several hundred courtesans and concubines, all dressed in silk and fed on fine grain and meat. Day and night he entertained himself with song and music, living in unmatched arrogance and extravagance.

sentences.zh: 與其弟渤海王奉慈俱為高祖所鄙，帝謂曰：「我怨仇有善，猶擢以不次，況於親戚而不委任？

translations.literal: Together with his younger brother Prince of Bohai Fengci he was both despised by Emperor Gaozu; the emperor said to them: "If even my enemies have merit I still promote them out of turn — how much more for kinsmen, yet I do not entrust you with office?
translations.idiomatic: He and his brother Prince Fengci of Bohai were both held in contempt by Gaozu. The emperor told them, "When even my enemies prove capable I promote them ahead of their turn. How much more should I trust my own kin—yet I do not?

sentences.zh: 聞汝等唯暱近小人，好為不軌，先王墳典，不聞習學。

translations.literal: I hear that you only draw close to petty men, delight in improper conduct, and have not been heard to study the classics of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that you keep company only with petty men, delight in misconduct, and never study the classics of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 今賜絹二百匹，可各買經史習讀，務為善事。」

translations.literal: Now I bestow two hundred bolts of silk — each of you may buy classics and histories to study, and strive to do good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: I grant you two hundred bolts of silk apiece. Buy the classics and histories and study them. Devote yourselves to worthy conduct.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年薨，贈開府儀同三司、荊州都督，謚曰恭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng he died; posthumously given Concurrent Grand Master of the Palace with Purse-Strings and metropolitan protector of Jing prefecture; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 671. He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Palace with Purse-Strings and Metropolitan Protector of Jingzhou, with the posthumous name Gong, meaning Respectful.

sentences.zh: 奉慈，武德初，封渤海王。

translations.literal: Fengci, at the beginning of Wude, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Fengci was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai at the start of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，累遷原州都督，薨，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: During Xianqing, through successive promotions he rose to metropolitan protector of Yuan prefecture; died; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era he rose to Metropolitan Protector of Yuanzhou. He died and was given the posthumous name Jing, meaning Reverent.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：無私於物，物亦公焉。

translations.literal: Commentary: The historiographer says: Without partiality toward things, things also become impartial.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The historiographer writes: When one shows no partiality toward others, others in turn show none toward him.

sentences.zh: 高祖才定中原，先封疏屬，致廬江為叛，神通爭功，封德彝論之於前，房玄齡譏之於後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu had just settled the Central Plain, he first enfeoffed distant kinsmen, causing Lujiang to rebel; Tong Shen fought for merit — Feng Deyi discussed it before, Fang Xuanling mocked it after.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had scarcely pacified the Central Plain when he enfeoffed distant kinsmen, provoking rebellion at Lujiang and quarrels over credit from Li Shentong. Feng Deyi criticized the policy early on, and Fang Xuanling mocked it later.

sentences.zh: 若河間機謀深沉，識度弘遠，縱虛舟而降蕭銑，飲妖血而平公祏，入朝定君臣之分，賣第為子孫之謀，善始令終，論功行賞，即無私矣。

translations.literal: As for the Prince of Hejian — his stratagems were deep and his vision broad; though he emptied his boats to surrender Xiao Xian and drank demon blood to pacify Fu Gongshi, entering court he fixed the distinction of ruler and subject, sold his mansion to plan for his descendants, good in beginning and fine in end, discussing merit and granting reward — that was without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaogong of Hejian was deep in counsel and broad in vision. He emptied his boats to take Xiao Xian and drank blood-tainted water to subdue Fu Gongshi. At court he upheld the proper order between sovereign and subject, sold his mansion to provide for his descendants, and ended as well as he began. When merit was weighed and rewards granted, he showed no partiality.

sentences.zh: 或問曰：「水變為血，信妖矣；

translations.literal: Someone asked: "Water turning into blood — truly an omen;
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "When water turned to blood, that was surely an evil omen.

sentences.zh: 竟成功而無咎者，何也？」

translations.literal: yet in the end he succeeded without blame — why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet he succeeded without suffering for it. Why?

sentences.zh: 答曰：河間節貫神明，志匡宗社，故妖不勝德明矣。

translations.literal: The reply was: The Prince of Hejian's integrity penetrated the divine; his will was to rescue the ancestral temple and altars — therefore the omen could not overcome his manifest virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: Prince Xiaogong of Hejian was integrity itself, devoted to restoring the dynasty. An evil omen could not overcome such manifest virtue.

sentences.zh: 道宗軍謀武勇，好學下賢，於群從之中，稱一時之傑。

translations.literal: Daozong in military planning and martial courage, loving learning and deferring to the worthy, among the clan cousins was called a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong combined military skill with courage, loved learning, and honored worthy men. Among the imperial cousins he was hailed as the outstanding man of his generation.

sentences.zh: 無忌、遂良銜不協之素，致千載之冤。

translations.literal: Wuji and Suiliang harbored old discord, causing a wrong that would last a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Suiliang, nursing old grudges against him, inflicted a wrong that would echo for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，無忌、遂良忠而獲罪，人皆哀之。

translations.literal: During Yonghui, Wuji and Suiliang were loyal yet fell into guilt; all people mourned them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era Wuji and Suiliang were loyal yet condemned, and all the realm mourned them.

sentences.zh: 殊不知誣陷劉洎、吳王恪於前，枉害道宗於後，天網不漏，不得其死也宜哉！

translations.literal: They little knew that before they had falsely implicated Liu Ji and Prince of Wu Ke, and afterward wrongly harmed Daozong — Heaven's net misses nothing; that they did not die a natural death was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: They forgot that they had already framed Liu Ji and Prince Ke of Wu, and later wrongfully destroyed Daozong. Heaven's net misses nothing. That they did not die natural deaths was only fitting!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：疏屬盡封，啟亂害公。

translations.literal: Praise says: Enfeoffing all distant kinsmen opened disorder and harmed the public good.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Enfeoffing every distant kinsman bred rebellion and harmed the state.

sentences.zh: 河間孝恭，獨稱軍功。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian Xiaogong alone was famed for military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Only Prince Xiaogong of Hejian won true distinction in arms.
